bay.en: I have seen the wicked in great power, and spreading himself like a green bay tree.
And in the third chariot white horses; and in the fourth chariot grisled and bay horses.

bdellium.en: And the gold of that land is good: there is bdellium and the onyx stone.
And the manna was as coriander seed, and the colour thereof as the colour of bdellium.

be.en: Grace be with you all. Amen.
Judge not, that ye be not judged.

beacon.en: One thousand shall flee at the rebuke of one; at the rebuke of five shall ye flee: till ye be left as a beacon upon the top of a mountain, and as an ensign on an hill.

beam.en: The beams of our house are cedar, and our rafters of fir.
And he built the inner court with three rows of hewed stone, and a row of cedar beams.

bean.en: Brought beds, and basons, and earthen vessels, and wheat, and barley, and flour, and parched corn, and beans, and lentiles, and parched pulse,

Take thou also unto thee wheat, and barley, and beans, and lentiles, and millet, and fitches, and put them in one vessel, and make thee bread thereof, according to the number of the days that thou shalt lie upon thy side, three hundred and ninety days shalt thou eat thereof.

bear.en: For every man shall bear his own burden.
If I bear witness of myself, my witness is not true.

beard.en: If a man or woman have a plague upon the head or the beard;
Ye shall not round the corners of your heads, neither shalt thou mar the corners of thy beard.

bearer.en: And Judah said, The strength of the bearers of burdens is decayed, and there is much rubbish; so that we are not able to build the wall.
And shall consume the glory of his forest, and of his fruitful field, both soul and body: and they shall be as when a standard-bearer fainteth.

bearing.en: Let us go forth therefore unto him without the camp, bearing his reproach.
When Leah saw that she had left bearing, she took Zilpah her maid, and gave her Jacob to wife.

beast.en: All sheep and oxen, yea, and the beasts of the field;
Who smote the firstborn of Egypt, both of man and beast.

beat.en: And they caught him, and beat him, and sent him away empty.
And he beat down the tower of Penuel, and slew the men of the city.

beaten.en: Their knops and their branches were of the same: all of it was one beaten work of pure gold.
For through the voice of the LORD shall the Assyrian be beaten down, which smote with a rod.

beating.en: And again he sent another; and him they killed, and many others; beating some, and killing some.
And the watchmen of Saul in Gibeah of Benjamin looked; and, behold, the multitude melted away, and they went on beating down one another.

beautiful.en: Leah was tender eyed; but Rachel was beautiful and well favoured.
Thou art beautiful, O my love, as Tirzah, comely as Jerusalem, terrible as an army with banners.

beautify.en: For the LORD taketh pleasure in his people: he will beautify the meek with salvation.
Blessed be the LORD God of our fathers, which hath put such a thing as this in the king’s heart, to beautify the house of the LORD which is in Jerusalem:

beauty.en: Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty, God hath shined.
Honour and majesty are before him: strength and beauty are in his sanctuary.

became.en: Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,
Which perished at Endor: they became as dung for the earth.

because.en: We love him, because he first loved us.
Of sin, because they believe not on me;

beckon.en: Simon Peter therefore beckoned to him, that he should ask who it should be of whom he spake.
Then Paul stood up, and beckoning with his hand said, Men of Israel, and ye that fear God, give audience.

become.en: Thy silver is become dross, thy wine mixed with water:
But speak thou the things which become sound doctrine:

bed.en: Jesus saith unto him, Rise, take up thy bed, and walk.
I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.

bedchamber.en: And one of his servants said, None, my lord, O king: but Elisha, the prophet that is in Israel, telleth the king of Israel the words that thou speakest in thy bedchamber.
Curse not the king, no not in thy thought; and curse not the rich in thy bedchamber: for a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which hath wings shall tell the matter.

bedstead.en: For only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of giants; behold, his bedstead was a bedstead of iron; is it not in Rabbath of the children of Ammon? nine cubits was the length thereof, and four cubits the breadth of it, after the cubit of a man.

bee.en: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the LORD shall hiss for the fly that is in the uttermost part of the rivers of Egypt, and for the bee that is in the land of Assyria.

beelzebub.en: But some of them said, He casteth out devils through Beelzebub the chief of the devils.
And if I by Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom do your sons cast them out? therefore shall they be your judges.

been.en: The LORD hath been sore displeased with your fathers.
Lord, thou hast been our dwelling place in all generations.

beer.en: And Jotham ran away, and fled, and went to Beer, and dwelt there, for fear of Abimelech his brother.
And from thence they went to Beer: that is the well whereof the LORD spake unto Moses, Gather the people together, and I will give them water.

beetle.en: Even these of them ye may eat; the locust after his kind, and the bald locust after his kind, and the beetle after his kind, and the grasshopper after his kind.

beeves.en: And thirty and six thousand beeves,
And threescore and twelve thousand beeves,

befall.en: There shall no evil befall thee, neither shall any plague come nigh thy dwelling.
And now, behold, I go bound in the spirit unto Jerusalem, not knowing the things that shall befall me there:

before.en: Behold, I have told you before.
Thou shalt have no other gods before me.

beforehand.en: Some men’s sins are open beforehand, going before to judgment; and some men they follow after.
Likewise also the good works of some are manifest beforehand; and they that are otherwise cannot be hid.

beforetime.en: And Joshua at that time turned back, and took Hazor, and smote the king thereof with the sword: for Hazor beforetime was the head of all those kingdoms.
(And the LORD gave Israel a saviour, so that they went out from under the hand of the Syrians: and the children of Israel dwelt in their tents, as beforetime.

beg.en: The sluggard will not plow by reason of the cold; therefore shall he beg in harvest, and have nothing.
Let his children be continually vagabonds, and beg: let them seek their bread also out of their desolate places.

begat.en: And Boaz begat Obed, and Obed begat Jesse,
And Hur begat Uri, and Uri begat Bezaleel.

beget.en: Thou shalt beget sons and daughters, but thou shalt not enjoy them; for they shall go into captivity.
If he beget a son that is a robber, a shedder of blood, and that doeth the like to any one of these things,

beggar.en: And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, which was laid at his gate, full of sores,
And it came to pass, that the beggar died, and was carried by the angels into Abraham’s bosom: the rich man also died, and was buried;

beggarly.en: But now, after that ye have known God, or rather are known of God, how turn ye again to the weak and beggarly elements, whereunto ye desire again to be in bondage?

begin.en: And shall begin to smite his fellowservants, and to eat and drink with the drunken;
Then shall they begin to say to the mountains, Fall on us; and to the hills, Cover us.

beginning.en: The same was in the beginning with God.
All these are the beginning of sorrows.

begotten.en: Hath the rain a father? or who hath begotten the drops of dew?
I beseech thee for my son Onesimus, whom I have begotten in my bonds:

beguile.en: And this I say, lest any man should beguile you with enticing words.
And the LORD God said unto the woman, What is this that thou hast done? And the woman said, The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.

beguiling.en: Having eyes full of adultery, and that cannot cease from sin; beguiling unstable souls: an heart they have exercised with covetous practices; cursed children:

begun.en: Are ye so foolish? having begun in the Spirit, are ye now made perfect by the flesh?
And the Jews undertook to do as they had begun, and as Mordecai had written unto them;

behalf.en: Suffer me a little, and I will shew thee that I have yet to speak on God’s behalf.
I thank my God always on your behalf, for the grace of God which is given you by Jesus Christ;

behave.en: And David behaved himself wisely in all his ways; and the LORD was with him.
Wherefore when Saul saw that he behaved himself very wisely, he was afraid of him.

behaviour.en: A bishop then must be blameless, the husband of one wife, vigilant, sober, of good behaviour, given to hospitality, apt to teach;
The aged women likewise, that they be in behaviour as becometh holiness, not false accusers, not given to much wine, teachers of good things;

behead.en: And he sent, and beheaded John in the prison.
But when Herod heard thereof, he said, It is John, whom I beheaded: he is risen from the dead.

beheld.en: And Israel beheld Joseph’s sons, and said, Who are these?
Upon this I awaked, and beheld; and my sleep was sweet unto me.

behemoth.en: Behold now behemoth, which I made with thee; he eateth grass as an ox.

behind.en: For I suppose I was not a whit behind the very chiefest apostles.
Seeing thou hatest instruction, and casteth my words behind thee.

behold.en: Behold, I have told you before.
Then said the Jews, Behold how he loved him!

beholding.en: The eyes of the LORD are in every place, beholding the evil and the good.
Turn away mine eyes from beholding vanity; and quicken thou me in thy way.

behove.en: And said unto them, Thus it is written, and thus it behoved Christ to suffer, and to rise from the dead the third day:

Wherefore in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren, that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest in things pertaining to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people.

being.en: So Job died, being old and full of days.
If so be that being clothed we shall not be found naked.

bekah.en: A bekah for every man, that is, half a shekel, after the shekel of the sanctuary, for every one that went to be numbered, from twenty years old and upward, for six hundred thousand and three thousand and five hundred and fifty men.

bel.en: Bel boweth down, Nebo stoopeth, their idols were upon the beasts, and upon the cattle: your carriages were heavy loaden; they are a burden to the weary beast.

And I will punish Bel in Babylon, and I will bring forth out of his mouth that which he hath swallowed up: and the nations shall not flow together any more unto him: yea, the wall of Babylon shall fall.

belch.en: Behold, they belch out with their mouth: swords are in their lips: for who, say they, doth hear?

belial.en: Now the sons of Eli were sons of Belial; they knew not the LORD.
And what concord hath Christ with Belial? or what part hath he that believeth with an infidel?

belie.en: They have belied the LORD, and said, It is not he; neither shall evil come upon us; neither shall we see sword nor famine:

belief.en: But we are bound to give thanks alway to God for you, brethren beloved of the Lord, because God hath from the beginning chosen you to salvation through sanctification of the Spirit and belief of the truth:

believe.en: And many believed on him there.
Of sin, because they believe not on me;

believer.en: And believers were the more added to the Lord, multitudes both of men and women.)
Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity.

believing.en: And all things, whatsoever ye shall ask in prayer, believing, ye shall receive.
And when he had brought them into his house, he set meat before them, and rejoiced, believing in God with all his house.

bell.en: A golden bell and a pomegranate, a golden bell and a pomegranate, upon the hem of the robe round about.
A bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, round about the hem of the robe to minister in; as the LORD commanded Moses.

bellow.en: Because ye were glad, because ye rejoiced, O ye destroyers of mine heritage, because ye are grown fat as the heifer at grass, and bellow as bulls;

bellows.en: The bellows are burned, the lead is consumed of the fire; the founder melteth in vain: for the wicked are not plucked away.

belly.en: Then Jonah prayed unto the LORD his God out of the fish’s belly,
For our soul is bowed down to the dust: our belly cleaveth unto the earth.

belong.en: Salvation belongeth unto the LORD: thy blessing is upon thy people. Selah.
God hath spoken once; twice have I heard this; that power belongeth unto God.

belonging.en: He that passeth by, and meddleth with strife belonging not to him, is like one that taketh a dog by the ears.
But unto the sons of Kohath he gave none: because the service of the sanctuary belonging unto them was that they should bear upon their shoulders.

beloved.en: Do not err, my beloved brethren.
Greet Amplias my beloved in the Lord.

bemoan.en: For who shall have pity upon thee, O Jerusalem? or who shall bemoan thee? or who shall go aside to ask how thou doest?
All ye that are about him, bemoan him; and all ye that know his name, say, How is the strong staff broken, and the beautiful rod!

ben.en: And it came to pass, when Ben-hadad heard this message, as he was drinking, he and the kings in the pavilions, that he said unto his servants, Set yourselves in array. And they set themselves in array against the city.

And with them their brethren of the second degree, Zechariah, Ben, and Jaaziel, and Shemiramoth, and Jehiel, and Unni, Eliab, and Benaiah, and Maaseiah, and Mattithiah, and Elipheleh, and Mikneiah, and Obededom, and Jeiel, the porters.

bench.en: Of the oaks of Bashan have they made thine oars; the company of the Ashurites have made thy benches of ivory, brought out of the isles of Chittim.

bend.en: Who whet their tongue like a sword, and bend their bows to shoot their arrows, even bitter words:
Let them melt away as waters which run continually: when he bendeth his bow to shoot his arrows, let them be as cut in pieces.

bending.en: The sons also of them that afflicted thee shall come bending unto thee; and all they that despised thee shall bow themselves down at the soles of thy feet; and they shall call thee, The city of the LORD, The Zion of the Holy One of Israel.

beneath.en: His roots shall be dried up beneath, and above shall his branch be cut off.
The way of life is above to the wise, that he may depart from hell beneath.

benefactor.en: And he said unto them, The kings of the Gentiles exercise lordship over them; and they that exercise authority upon them are called benefactors.

benefit.en: Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits:
What shall I render unto the LORD for all his benefits toward me?

benevolence.en: Let the husband render unto the wife due benevolence: and likewise also the wife unto the husband.

benjamite.en: And Shimei the son of Gera, a Benjamite, which was of Bahurim, hasted and came down with the men of Judah to meet king David.
The ninth captain for the ninth month was Abiezer the Anetothite, of the Benjamites: and in his course were twenty and four thousand.

bent.en: He hath bent his bow, and set me as a mark for the arrow.
If he turn not, he will whet his sword; he hath bent his bow, and made it ready.

bere.en: Wherefore the well was called Beerlahairoi; behold, it is between Kadesh and Bered.
And the sons of Ephraim; Shuthelah, and Bered his son, and Tahath his son, and Eladah his son, and Tahath his son,

bereave.en: Therefore thou shalt devour men no more, neither bereave thy nations any more, saith the Lord GOD.
Thus saith the Lord GOD; Because they say unto you, Thou land devourest up men, and hast bereaved thy nations;

beryl.en: And the fourth row a beryl, and an onyx, and a jasper: they shall be set in gold in their inclosings.
His hands are as gold rings set with the beryl: his belly is as bright ivory overlaid with sapphires.

beseech.en: Wherefore I beseech you, be ye followers of me.
And he said, I beseech thee, shew me thy glory.

beseeching.en: And when Jesus was entered into Capernaum, there came unto him a centurion, beseeching him,
And when he heard of Jesus, he sent unto him the elders of the Jews, beseeching him that he would come and heal his servant.

beset.en: Thou hast beset me behind and before, and laid thine hand upon me.
Many bulls have compassed me: strong bulls of Bashan have beset me round.

beside.en: I, even I, am the LORD; and beside me there is no saviour.
The king of Jericho, one; the king of Ai, which is beside Bethel, one;

besides.en: And I baptized also the household of Stephanas: besides, I know not whether I baptized any other.
And Jehoshaphat said, Is there not here a prophet of the LORD besides, that we might enquire of him?

besiege.en: So the city was besieged unto the eleventh year of king Zedekiah.
And the city was besieged unto the eleventh year of king Zedekiah.

besom.en: I will also make it a possession for the bittern, and pools of water: and I will sweep it with the besom of destruction, saith the LORD of hosts.

besought.en: And I besought the LORD at that time, saying,
And I besought thy disciples to cast him out; and they could not.

best.en: But covet earnestly the best gifts: and yet shew I unto you a more excellent way.
Moreover the king made a great throne of ivory, and overlaid it with the best gold.

bestead.en: And they shall pass through it, hardly bestead and hungry: and it shall come to pass, that when they shall be hungry, they shall fret themselves, and curse their king and their God, and look upward.

bestir.en: And let it be, when thou hearest the sound of a going in the tops of the mulberry trees, that then thou shalt bestir thyself: for then shall the LORD go out before thee, to smite the host of the Philistines.

bestow.en: Greet Mary, who bestowed much labour on us.
I am afraid of you, lest I have bestowed upon you labour in vain.

bethel.en: And Betharabah, and Zemaraim, and Bethel,
The king of Makkedah, one; the king of Bethel, one;

bethink.en: Yet if they bethink themselves in the land whither they are carried captive, and turn and pray unto thee in the land of their captivity, saying, We have sinned, we have done amiss, and have dealt wickedly;

Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent, and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness;

bethlehem.en: He built even Bethlehem, and Etam, and Tekoa,
Then died Ibzan, and was buried at Bethlehem.

bethlehemite.en: And Saul said to him, Whose son art thou, thou young man? And David answered, I am the son of thy servant Jesse the Bethlehemite.

And there was again a battle in Gob with the Philistines, where Elhanan the son of Jaareoregim, a Bethlehemite, slew the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the staff of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.

betimes.en: If thou wouldest seek unto God betimes, and make thy supplication to the Almighty;
He that spareth his rod hateth his son: but he that loveth him chasteneth him betimes.

betray.en: And from that time he sought opportunity to betray him.
Rise up, let us go; lo, he that betrayeth me is at hand.

betrayer.en: Which of the prophets have not your fathers persecuted? and they have slain them which shewed before of the coming of the Just One; of whom ye have been now the betrayers and murderers:

betroth.en: I will even betroth thee unto me in faithfulness: and thou shalt know the LORD.
For he found her in the field, and the betrothed damsel cried, and there was none to save her.

better.en: Open rebuke is better than secret love.
By so much was Jesus made a surety of a better testament.

between.en: Issachar is a strong ass couching down between two burdens:
One is so near to another, that no air can come between them.

betwixt.en: Neither is there any daysman betwixt us, that might lay his hand upon us both.
A bundle of myrrh is my well-beloved unto me; he shall lie all night betwixt my breasts.

bewail.en: And all wept, and bewailed her: but he said, Weep not; she is not dead, but sleepeth.
And there followed him a great company of people, and of women, which also bewailed and lamented him.

beware.en: Beware of dogs, beware of evil workers, beware of the concision.
Beware therefore, lest that come upon you, which is spoken of in the prophets;

bewitch.en: And to him they had regard, because that of long time he had bewitched them with sorceries.
O foolish Galatians, who hath bewitched you, that ye should not obey the truth, before whose eyes Jesus Christ hath been evidently set forth, crucified among you?

bewray.en: Whoso is partner with a thief hateth his own soul: he heareth cursing, and bewrayeth it not.
Whosoever hideth her hideth the wind, and the ointment of his right hand, which bewrayeth itself.

beyond.en: And Israel journeyed, and spread his tent beyond the tower of Edar.
These things were done in Bethabara beyond Jordan, where John was baptizing.

bid.en: Go ye therefore into the highways, and as many as ye shall find, bid to the marriage.
And Peter answered him and said, Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee on the water.

bidden.en: For I say unto you, That none of those men which were bidden shall taste of my supper.
Then saith he to his servants, The wedding is ready, but they which were bidden were not worthy.

bidding.en: Then Ahimelech answered the king, and said, And who is so faithful among all thy servants as David, which is the king’s son in law, and goeth at thy bidding, and is honourable in thine house?

bier.en: And he came and touched the bier: and they that bare him stood still. And he said, Young man, I say unto thee, Arise.
And David said to Joab, and to all the people that were with him, Rend your clothes, and gird you with sackcloth, and mourn before Abner. And king David himself followed the bier.

bill.en: And they said, Moses suffered to write a bill of divorcement, and to put her away.
And he said, An hundred measures of oil. And he said unto him, Take thy bill, and sit down quickly, and write fifty.

billow.en: Deep calleth unto deep at the noise of thy waterspouts: all thy waves and thy billows are gone over me.
For thou hadst cast me into the deep, in the midst of the seas; and the floods compassed me about: all thy billows and thy waves passed over me.

bind.en: Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.
He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds.

binding.en: And I persecuted this way unto the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women.
Every vow, and every binding oath to afflict the soul, her husband may establish it, or her husband may make it void.

bird.en: Of all clean birds ye shall eat.
Mine enemies chased me sore, like a bird, without cause.

birth.en: And as Jesus passed by, he saw a man which was blind from his birth.
And thou shalt have joy and gladness; and many shall rejoice at his birth.

birthday.en: But when Herod’s birthday was kept, the daughter of Herodias danced before them, and pleased Herod.
And when a convenient day was come, that Herod on his birthday made a supper to his lords, high captains, and chief estates of Galilee;

birthright.en: And Jacob said, Sell me this day thy birthright.
And Esau said, Behold, I am at the point to die: and what profit shall this birthright do to me?

bishop.en: This is a true saying, If a man desire the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work.
For ye were as sheep going astray; but are now returned unto the Shepherd and Bishop of your souls.

bit.en: At the last it biteth like a serpent, and stingeth like an adder.
Behold, we put bits in the horses’ mouths, that they may obey us; and we turn about their whole body.

bite.en: Surely the serpent will bite without enchantment; and a babbler is no better.
But if ye bite and devour one another, take heed that ye be not consumed one of another.

bitten.en: And Moses made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a pole, and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived.
And the LORD said unto Moses, Make thee a fiery serpent, and set it upon a pole: and it shall come to pass, that every one that is bitten, when he looketh upon it, shall live.

bitter.en: Husbands, love your wives, and be not bitter against them.
But her end is bitter as wormwood, sharp as a two-edged sword.

bitterly.en: And Peter went out, and wept bitterly.
Behold, their valiant ones shall cry without: the ambassadors of peace shall weep bitterly.

bittern.en: I will also make it a possession for the bittern, and pools of water: and I will sweep it with the besom of destruction, saith the LORD of hosts.
But the cormorant and the bittern shall possess it; the owl also and the raven shall dwell in it: and he shall stretch out upon it the line of confusion, and the stones of emptiness.

bitterness.en: Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness:
He will not suffer me to take my breath, but filleth me with bitterness.

black.en: My skin is black upon me, and my bones are burned with heat.
In the twilight, in the evening, in the black and dark night:

blackish.en: Which are blackish by reason of the ice, and wherein the snow is hid:

blackness.en: I clothe the heavens with blackness, and I make sackcloth their covering.
Before their face the people shall be much pained: all faces shall gather blackness.

blade.en: Then let mine arm fall from my shoulder blade, and mine arm be broken from the bone.
But when the blade was sprung up, and brought forth fruit, then appeared the tares also.

blain.en: And it shall become small dust in all the land of Egypt, and shall be a boil breaking forth with blains upon man, and upon beast, throughout all the land of Egypt.
And they took ashes of the furnace, and stood before Pharaoh; and Moses sprinkled it up toward heaven; and it became a boil breaking forth with blains upon man, and upon beast.

blame.en: Giving no offence in any thing, that the ministry be not blamed:
Avoiding this, that no man should blame us in this abundance which is administered by us:

blameless.en: And these things give in charge, that they may be blameless.
And the men said unto her, We will be blameless of this thine oath which thou hast made us swear.

blaspheme.en: Do not they blaspheme that worthy name by the which ye are called?
And, behold, certain of the scribes said within themselves, This man blasphemeth.

blasphemer.en: For ye have brought hither these men, which are neither robbers of churches, nor yet blasphemers of your goddess.
Who was before a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and injurious: but I obtained mercy, because I did it ignorantly in unbelief.

blasphemous.en: Then they suborned men, which said, We have heard him speak blasphemous words against Moses, and against God.
And set up false witnesses, which said, This man ceaseth not to speak blasphemous words against this holy place, and the law:

blasphemously.en: And many other things blasphemously spake they against him.

blasphemy.en: Why doth this man thus speak blasphemies? who can forgive sins but God only?
Ye have heard the blasphemy: what think ye? And they all condemned him to be guilty of death.

blast.en: By the blast of God they perish, and by the breath of his nostrils are they consumed.
Behold, I will send a blast upon him, and he shall hear a rumour, and return to his own land; and I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land.

blasted.en: And, behold, seven thin ears and blasted with the east wind sprung up after them.
And, behold, seven ears, withered, thin, and blasted with the east wind, sprung up after them:

blasting.en: I smote you with blasting and with mildew and with hail in all the labours of your hands; yet ye turned not to me, saith the LORD.

I have smitten you with blasting and mildew: when your gardens and your vineyards and your fig trees and your olive trees increased, the palmerworm devoured them: yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the LORD.

blaze.en: But he went out, and began to publish it much, and to blaze abroad the matter, insomuch that Jesus could no more openly enter into the city, but was without in desert places: and they came to him from every quarter.

bleating.en: And Samuel said, What meaneth then this bleating of the sheep in mine ears, and the lowing of the oxen which I hear?
Why abodest thou among the sheepfolds, to hear the bleatings of the flocks? For the divisions of Reuben there were great searchings of heart.

blemish.en: But with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot:
And if he bring a lamb for a sin offering, he shall bring it a female without blemish.

bless.en: The LORD bless thee, and keep thee:
Bless them which persecute you: bless, and curse not.

blessed.en: Blessed shall be thy basket and thy store.
Blessed art thou, O LORD: teach me thy statutes.

blessedness.en: Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works,
Cometh this blessedness then upon the circumcision only, or upon the uncircumcision also? for we say that faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness.

blessing.en: Behold, I set before you this day a blessing and a curse;
And were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God. Amen.

blew.en: And the sea arose by reason of a great wind that blew.
But the Spirit of the LORD came upon Gideon, and he blew a trumpet; and Abiezer was gathered after him.

blind.en: Hear, ye deaf; and look, ye blind, that ye may see.
I was eyes to the blind, and feet was I to the lame.

blindfold.en: And when they had blindfolded him, they struck him on the face, and asked him, saying, Prophesy, who is it that smote thee?

blindness.en: The LORD shall smite thee with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart:
And they smote the men that were at the door of the house with blindness, both small and great: so that they wearied themselves to find the door.

block.en: I will consume man and beast; I will consume the fowls of the heaven, and the fishes of the sea, and the stumbling blocks with the wicked: and I will cut off man from off the land, saith the LORD.

Again, When a righteous man doth turn from his righteousness, and commit iniquity, and I lay a stumbling-block before him, he shall die: because thou hast not given him warning, he shall die in his sin, and his righteousness which he hath done shall not be remembered; but his blood will I require at thine hand.

blood.en: Their feet are swift to shed blood:
He turned their waters into blood, and slew their fish.

bloodthirsty.en: The bloodthirsty hate the upright: but the just seek his soul.

bloody.en: Gather not my soul with sinners, nor my life with bloody men:
Deliver me from the workers of iniquity, and save me from bloody men.

bloom.en: And it came to pass, that on the morrow Moses went into the tabernacle of witness; and, behold, the rod of Aaron for the house of Levi was budded, and brought forth buds, and bloomed blossoms, and yielded almonds.

blossom.en: Behold the day, behold, it is come: the morning is gone forth; the rod hath blossomed, pride hath budded.
The wilderness and the solitary place shall be glad for them; and the desert shall rejoice, and blossom as the rose.

blot.en: Hide thy face from my sins, and blot out all mine iniquities.
And the LORD said unto Moses, Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book.

blow.en: Blow the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly:
Remove thy stroke away from me: I am consumed by the blow of thine hand.

blown.en: Shall a trumpet be blown in the city, and the people not be afraid? shall there be evil in a city, and the LORD hath not done it?
They have blown the trumpet, even to make all ready; but none goeth to the battle: for my wrath is upon all the multitude thereof.

blue.en: And thou shalt make the robe of the ephod all of blue.
And he made the robe of the ephod of woven work, all of blue.

blueness.en: The blueness of a wound cleanseth away evil: so do stripes the inward parts of the belly.

blunt.en: If the iron be blunt, and he do not whet the edge, then must he put to more strength: but wisdom is profitable to direct.

blush.en: And said, O my God, I am ashamed and blush to lift up my face to thee, my God: for our iniquities are increased over our head, and our trespass is grown up unto the heavens.

Were they ashamed when they had committed abomination? nay, they were not at all ashamed, neither could they blush: therefore they shall fall among them that fall: at the time that I visit them they shall be cast down, saith the LORD.

boanerges.en: And James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James; and he surnamed them Boanerges, which is, The sons of thunder:

boar.en: The boar out of the wood doth waste it, and the wild beast of the field doth devour it.

board.en: And for the sides of the tabernacle westward he made six boards.
And he made boards for the tabernacle of shittim wood, standing up.

boast.en: Not of works, lest any man should boast.
In God we boast all the day long, and praise thy name for ever. Selah.

boaster.en: Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents,
For men shall be lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy,

boasting.en: But now ye rejoice in your boastings: all such rejoicing is evil.
Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith.

boat.en: Then the soldiers cut off the ropes of the boat, and let her fall off.
And running under a certain island which is called Clauda, we had much work to come by the boat:

bodily.en: For in him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily.
For his letters, say they, are weighty and powerful; but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech contemptible.

body.en: But he spake of the temple of his body.
For the body is not one member, but many.

boil.en: The flesh also, in which, even in the skin thereof, was a boil, and is healed,
He maketh the deep to boil like a pot: he maketh the sea like a pot of ointment.

boiled.en: My bowels boiled, and rested not: the days of affliction prevented me.
So we boiled my son, and did eat him: and I said unto her on the next day, Give thy son, that we may eat him: and she hath hid her son.

boiling.en: And there was a row of building round about in them, round about them four, and it was made with boiling places under the rows round about.

boisterous.en: But when he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried, saying, Lord, save me.

bold.en: The wicked flee when no man pursueth: but the righteous are bold as a lion.
Wherefore, though I might be much bold in Christ to enjoin thee that which is convenient,

boldly.en: For which I am an ambassador in bonds: that therein I may speak boldly, as I ought to speak.
So that we may boldly say, The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me.

boldness.en: In whom we have boldness and access with confidence by the faith of him.
Having therefore, brethren, boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus,

boll.en: And the flax and the barley was smitten: for the barley was in the ear, and the flax was bolled.

bolster.en: And when the messengers were come in, behold, there was an image in the bed, with a pillow of goats’ hair for his bolster.
And Michal took an image, and laid it in the bed, and put a pillow of goats’ hair for his bolster, and covered it with a cloth.

bolt.en: Then he called his servant that ministered unto him, and said, Put now this woman out from me, and bolt the door after her.
And she had a garment of divers colours upon her: for with such robes were the king’s daughters that were virgins apparelled. Then his servant brought her out, and bolted the door after her.

bon.en: He keepeth all his bones: not one of them is broken.
I may tell all my bones: they look and stare upon me.

bond.en: Endeavouring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
He looseth the bond of kings, and girdeth their loins with a girdle.

bondage.en: Even so we, when we were children, were in bondage under the elements of the world:
And the Egyptians evil entreated us, and afflicted us, and laid upon us hard bondage:

bondmaid.en: For it is written, that Abraham had two sons, the one by a bondmaid, the other by a freewoman.
Both thy bondmen, and thy bondmaids, which thou shalt have, shall be of the heathen that are round about you; of them shall ye buy bondmen and bondmaids.

bondman.en: And thou shalt remember that thou wast a bondman in Egypt: and thou shalt observe and do these statutes.
And thou shalt remember that thou wast a bondman in the land of Egypt: therefore I command thee to do this thing.

bondwoman.en: So then, brethren, we are not children of the bondwoman, but of the free.
And also of the son of the bondwoman will I make a nation, because he is thy seed.

bone.en: By long forbearing is a prince persuaded, and a soft tongue breaketh the bone.
Then let mine arm fall from my shoulder blade, and mine arm be broken from the bone.

bonnet.en: The bonnets, and the ornaments of the legs, and the headbands, and the tablets, and the earrings,
And a mitre of fine linen, and goodly bonnets of fine linen, and linen breeches of fine twined linen,

book.en: The burden of Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.
Oh that my words were now written! oh that they were printed in a book!

booth.en: He buildeth his house as a moth, and as a booth that the keeper maketh.
Ye shall dwell in booths seven days; all that are Israelites born shall dwell in booths:

booty.en: Shall they not rise up suddenly that shall bite thee, and awake that shall vex thee, and thou shalt be for booties unto them?
And the booty, being the rest of the prey which the men of war had caught, was six hundred thousand and seventy thousand and five thousand sheep,

border.en: And Mejarkon, and Rakkon, with the border before Japho.
We will make thee borders of gold with studs of silver.

bore.en: Canst thou put an hook into his nose? or bore his jaw through with a thorn?
And Tamar his daughter in law bore him Pharez and Zerah. All the sons of Judah were five.

born.en: And Canaan begat Sidon his first born, and Heth,
Yet man is born unto trouble, as the sparks fly upward.

borne.en: Thou hast borne thy lewdness and thine abominations, saith the LORD.
Because for thy sake I have borne reproach; shame hath covered my face.

borrow.en: Give to him that asketh thee, and from him that would borrow of thee turn not thou away.
The wicked borroweth, and payeth not again: but the righteous sheweth mercy, and giveth.

borrower.en: The rich ruleth over the poor, and the borrower is servant to the lender.

And it shall be, as with the people, so with the priest; as with the servant, so with his master; as with the maid, so with her mistress; as with the buyer, so with the seller; as with the lender, so with the borrower; as with the taker of usury, so with the giver of usury to him.

bosom.en: Can a man take fire in his bosom, and his clothes not be burned?
A gift in secret pacifieth anger: and a reward in the bosom strong wrath.

boss.en: He runneth upon him, even on his neck, upon the thick bosses of his bucklers:

botch.en: The LORD will smite thee with the botch of Egypt, and with the emerods, and with the scab, and with the itch, whereof thou canst not be healed.
The LORD shall smite thee in the knees, and in the legs, with a sore botch that cannot be healed, from the sole of thy foot unto the top of thy head.

both.en: Both low and high, rich and poor, together.
Both young men, and maidens; old men, and children:

bottle.en: But new wine must be put into new bottles; and both are preserved.
Then shalt thou break the bottle in the sight of the men that go with thee,

bottom.en: The depths have covered them: they sank into the bottom as a stone.
And the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom.

bottomless.en: And I saw an angel come down from heaven, having the key of the bottomless pit and a great chain in his hand.
And the fifth angel sounded, and I saw a star fall from heaven unto the earth: and to him was given the key of the bottomless pit.

bough.en: She sent out her boughs unto the sea, and her branches unto the river.
Yet through the scent of water it will bud, and bring forth boughs like a plant.

bought.en: Ye are bought with a price; be not ye the servants of men.
And they took counsel, and bought with them the potter’s field, to bury strangers in.

bound.en: The iniquity of Ephraim is bound up; his sin is hid.
Now Annas had sent him bound unto Caiaphas the high priest.

bountiful.en: The vile person shall be no more called liberal, nor the churl said to be bountiful.
He that hath a bountiful eye shall be blessed; for he giveth of his bread to the poor.

bounty.en: And king Solomon gave unto the queen of Sheba all her desire, whatsoever she asked, beside that which Solomon gave her of his royal bounty. So she turned and went to her own country, she and her servants.

Therefore I thought it necessary to exhort the brethren, that they would go before unto you, and make up beforehand your bounty, whereof ye had notice before, that the same might be ready, as a matter of bounty, and not as of covetousness.

bow.en: And the man bowed down his head, and worshipped the LORD.
He hath bent his bow, and set me as a mark for the arrow.

bowel.en: Ye are not straitened in us, but ye are straitened in your own bowels.
My bowels boiled, and rested not: the days of affliction prevented me.

bowing.en: They have now compassed us in our steps: they have set their eyes bowing down to the earth;
And they smote him on the head with a reed, and did spit upon him, and bowing their knees worshipped him.

bowl.en: And two olive trees by it, one upon the right side of the bowl, and the other upon the left side thereof.
Or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern.

bowls.en: And in the candlestick were four bowls made like almonds, his knops, and his flowers:
And in the candlestick shall be four bowls made like unto almonds, with their knops and their flowers.

box.en: There came unto him a woman having an alabaster box of very precious ointment, and poured it on his head, as he sat at meat.
And, behold, a woman in the city, which was a sinner, when she knew that Jesus sat at meat in the Pharisee’s house, brought an alabaster box of ointment,

boy.en: And the streets of the city shall be full of boys and girls playing in the streets thereof.
And the boys grew: and Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field; and Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents.

bracelet.en: The chains, and the bracelets, and the mufflers,
I decked thee also with ornaments, and I put bracelets upon thy hands, and a chain on thy neck.

brake.en: And brake up for it my decreed place, and set bars and doors,
And I brake the jaws of the wicked, and plucked the spoil out of his teeth.

bramble.en: Then said all the trees unto the bramble, Come thou, and reign over us.
For every tree is known by his own fruit. For of thorns men do not gather figs, nor of a bramble bush gather they grapes.

branch.en: She sent out her boughs unto the sea, and her branches unto the river.
He is green before the sun, and his branch shooteth forth in his garden.

brand.en: And the LORD said unto Satan, The LORD rebuke thee, O Satan; even the LORD that hath chosen Jerusalem rebuke thee: is not this a brand plucked out of the fire?
And when he had set the brands on fire, he let them go into the standing corn of the Philistines, and burnt up both the shocks, and also the standing corn, with the vineyards and olives.

brandish.en: Yea, I will make many people amazed at thee, and their kings shall be horribly afraid for thee, when I shall brandish my sword before them; and they shall tremble at every moment, every man for his own life, in the day of thy fall.

brasen.en: The brasen altar, and his grate of brass, his staves, and all his vessels, the laver and his foot,
And he made for the altar a brasen grate of network under the compass thereof beneath unto the midst of it.

brass.en: He esteemeth iron as straw, and brass as rotten wood.
Provide neither gold, nor silver, nor brass in your purses,

bravery.en: In that day the Lord will take away the bravery of their tinkling ornaments about their feet, and their cauls, and their round tires like the moon,

brawler.en: To speak evil of no man, to be no brawlers, but gentle, shewing all meekness unto all men.
Not given to wine, no striker, not greedy of filthy lucre; but patient, not a brawler, not covetous;

brawling.en: It is better to dwell in a corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman in a wide house.
It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman and in a wide house.

bray.en: Doth the wild ass bray when he hath grass? or loweth the ox over his fodder?
Among the bushes they brayed; under the nettles they were gathered together.

breach.en: He breaketh me with breach upon breach, he runneth upon me like a giant.
A wholesome tongue is a tree of life: but perverseness therein is a breach in the spirit.

bread.en: I am that bread of life.
Give us this day our daily bread.

breadth.en: And the breadth of the court on the east side eastward shall be fifty cubits.
Hast thou perceived the breadth of the earth? declare if thou knowest it all.

break.en: Shall iron break the northern iron and the steel?
Thou breakest the ships of Tarshish with an east wind.

breaker.en: For circumcision verily profiteth, if thou keep the law: but if thou be a breaker of the law, thy circumcision is made uncircumcision.
The breaker is come up before them: they have broken up, and have passed through the gate, and are gone out by it: and their king shall pass before them, and the LORD on the head of them.

breast.en: Thy two breasts are like two young roes that are twins.
He then lying on Jesus’ breast saith unto him, Lord, who is it?

breastplate.en: Onyx stones, and stones to be set in the ephod, and in the breastplate.
And onyx stones, and stones to be set for the ephod, and for the breastplate.

breath.en: His breath kindleth coals, and a flame goeth out of his mouth.
Let every thing that hath breath praise the LORD. Praise ye the LORD.

breathe.en: Deliver me not over unto the will of mine enemies: for false witnesses are risen up against me, and such as breathe out cruelty.
And they smote all the souls that were therein with the edge of the sword, utterly destroying them: there was not any left to breathe: and he burnt Hazor with fire.

breathing.en: Thou hast heard my voice: hide not thine ear at my breathing, at my cry.
And Saul, yet breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, went unto the high priest,

bred.en: Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto Moses; but some of them left of it until the morning, and it bred worms, and stank: and Moses was wroth with them.

breeches.en: And a mitre of fine linen, and goodly bonnets of fine linen, and linen breeches of fine twined linen,
And thou shalt make them linen breeches to cover their nakedness; from the loins even unto the thighs they shall reach:

breed.en: Butter of kine, and milk of sheep, with fat of lambs, and rams of the breed of Bashan, and goats, with the fat of kidneys of wheat; and thou didst drink the pure blood of the grape.

Bring forth with thee every living thing that is with thee, of all flesh, both of fowl, and of cattle, and of every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth; that they may breed abundantly in the earth, and be fruitful, and multiply upon the earth.

breeding.en: Therefore as I live, saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, Surely Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah, even the breeding of nettles, and saltpits, and a perpetual desolation: the residue of my people shall spoil them, and the remnant of my people shall possess them.

brethren.en: Do not err, my beloved brethren.

bribe.en: In whose hands is mischief, and their right hand is full of bribes.
And his sons walked not in his ways, but turned aside after lucre, and took bribes, and perverted judgment.

bribery.en: For the congregation of hypocrites shall be desolate, and fire shall consume the tabernacles of bribery.

brick.en: Go therefore now, and work; for there shall no straw be given you, yet shall ye deliver the tale of bricks.
Ye shall no more give the people straw to make brick, as heretofore: let them go and gather straw for themselves.

brickkiln.en: Draw thee waters for the siege, fortify thy strong holds: go into clay, and tread the morter, make strong the brickkiln.
Take great stones in thine hand, and hide them in the clay in the brickkiln, which is at the entry of Pharaoh’s house in Tahpanhes, in the sight of the men of Judah;

bride.en: Can a maid forget her ornaments, or a bride her attire? yet my people have forgotten me days without number.
And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.

bridechamber.en: And he said unto them, Can ye make the children of the bridechamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them?
And Jesus said unto them, Can the children of the bridechamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them? as long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.

bridegroom.en: While the bridegroom tarried, they all slumbered and slept.
And at midnight there was a cry made, Behold, the bridegroom cometh; go ye out to meet him.

bridle.en: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, and a rod for the fool’s back.
Who can discover the face of his garment? or who can come to him with his double bridle?

briefly.en: By Silvanus, a faithful brother unto you, as I suppose, I have written briefly, exhorting, and testifying that this is the true grace of God wherein ye stand.

For this, Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt not kill, Thou shalt not steal, Thou shalt not bear false witness, Thou shalt not covet; and if there be any other commandment, it is briefly comprehended in this saying, namely, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.

brier.en: With arrows and with bows shall men come thither; because all the land shall become briers and thorns.
But that which beareth thorns and briers is rejected, and is nigh unto cursing; whose end is to be burned.

brigandine.en: Harness the horses; and get up, ye horsemen, and stand forth with your helmets; furbish the spears, and put on the brigandines.
Against him that bendeth let the archer bend his bow, and against him that lifteth himself up in his brigandine: and spare ye not her young men; destroy ye utterly all her host.

bright.en: And for a rising, and for a scab, and for a bright spot:
Also by watering he wearieth the thick cloud: he scattereth his bright cloud:

brightness.en: Through the brightness before him were coals of fire kindled.
If I beheld the sun when it shined, or the moon walking in brightness;

brim.en: Jesus saith unto them, Fill the waterpots with water. And they filled them up to the brim.
And it was an hand breadth thick, and the brim thereof was wrought like the brim of a cup, with flowers of lilies: it contained two thousand baths.

brimstone.en: Then the LORD rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the LORD out of heaven;
But the same day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed them all.

bring.en: He said, Bring them hither to me.
Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance:

bringer.en: And he that was over the house, and he that was over the city, the elders also, and the bringers up of the children, sent to Jehu, saying, We are thy servants, and will do all that thou shalt bid us; we will not make any king: do thou that which is good in thine eyes.

brink.en: And he said unto me, Son of man, hast thou seen this? Then he brought me, and caused me to return to the brink of the river.
And, behold, seven other kine came up after them out of the river, ill favoured and leanfleshed; and stood by the other kine upon the brink of the river.

broad.en: I have seen an end of all perfection: but thy commandment is exceeding broad.
And the arches round about were five and twenty cubits long, and five cubits broad.

broid.en: In like manner also, that women adorn themselves in modest apparel, with shamefacedness and sobriety; not with broided hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly array;

broider.en: And tookest thy broidered garments, and coveredst them: and thou hast set mine oil and mine incense before them.
I clothed thee also with broidered work, and shod thee with badgers’ skin, and I girded thee about with fine linen, and I covered thee with silk.

broil.en: And they gave him a piece of a broiled fish, and of an honeycomb.

broken.en: He keepeth all his bones: not one of them is broken.
He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds.

brood.en: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, which killest the prophets, and stonest them that are sent unto thee; how often would I have gathered thy children together, as a hen doth gather her brood under her wings, and ye would not!

brook.en: Hurai of the brooks of Gaash, Abiel the Arbathite,
Benaiah the Pirathonite, Hiddai of the brooks of Gaash,

broth.en: Which remain among the graves, and lodge in the monuments, which eat swine’s flesh, and broth of abominable things is in their vessels;
And the angel of God said unto him, Take the flesh and the unleavened cakes, and lay them upon this rock, and pour out the broth. And he did so.

brother.en: I am a brother to dragons, and a companion to owls.
Jesus saith unto her, Thy brother shall rise again.

brotherhood.en: Honour all men. Love the brotherhood. Fear God. Honour the king.
Then I cut asunder mine other staff, even Bands, that I might break the brotherhood between Judah and Israel.

brotherly.en: And to godliness brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness charity.

brow.en: Because I knew that thou art obstinate, and thy neck is an iron sinew, and thy brow brass;
And rose up, and thrust him out of the city, and led him unto the brow of the hill whereon their city was built, that they might cast him down headlong.

brown.en: And Jacob did separate the lambs, and set the faces of the flocks toward the ringstraked, and all the brown in the flock of Laban; and he put his own flocks by themselves, and put them not unto Laban’s cattle.

I will pass through all thy flock to day, removing from thence all the speckled and spotted cattle, and all the brown cattle among the sheep, and the spotted and speckled among the goats: and of such shall be my hire.

bruise.en: For thus saith the LORD, Thy bruise is incurable, and thy wound is grievous.
A bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench, till he send forth judgment unto victory.

bruit.en: Behold, the noise of the bruit is come, and a great commotion out of the north country, to make the cities of Judah desolate, and a den of dragons.
There is no healing of thy bruise; thy wound is grievous: all that hear the bruit of thee shall clap the hands over thee: for upon whom hath not thy wickedness passed continually?

brute.en: But these speak evil of those things which they know not: but what they know naturally, as brute beasts, in those things they corrupt themselves.
But these, as natural brute beasts, made to be taken and destroyed, speak evil of the things that they understand not; and shall utterly perish in their own corruption;

brutish.en: A brutish man knoweth not; neither doth a fool understand this.
Understand, ye brutish among the people: and ye fools, when will ye be wise?

bucket.en: Behold, the nations are as a drop of a bucket, and are counted as the small dust of the balance: behold, he taketh up the isles as a very little thing.
He shall pour the water out of his buckets, and his seed shall be in many waters, and his king shall be higher than Agag, and his kingdom shall be exalted.

buckler.en: Order ye the buckler and shield, and draw near to battle.
Take hold of shield and buckler, and stand up for mine help.

bud.en: Yet through the scent of water it will bud, and bring forth boughs like a plant.
There will I make the horn of David to bud: I have ordained a lamp for mine anointed.

buffet.en: Then did they spit in his face, and buffeted him; and others smote him with the palms of their hands,
Even unto this present hour we both hunger, and thirst, and are naked, and are buffeted, and have no certain dwellingplace;

build.en: Jerusalem is builded as a city that is compact together:
They build up Zion with blood, and Jerusalem with iniquity.

builder.en: The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner.
For he looked for a city which hath foundations, whose builder and maker is God.

building.en: But Solomon was building his own house thirteen years, and he finished all his house.
For we are labourers together with God: ye are God’s husbandry, ye are God’s building.

built.en: But Solomon built him an house.
So Solomon built the house, and finished it.

bull.en: Will I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?
Many bulls have compassed me: strong bulls of Bashan have beset me round.

bullock.en: And they slew a bullock, and brought the child to Eli.
I will take no bullock out of thy house, nor he goats out of thy folds.

bulrush.en: And when she could not longer hide him, she took for him an ark of bulrushes, and daubed it with slime and with pitch, and put the child therein; and she laid it in the flags by the river’s brink.

Is it such a fast that I have chosen? a day for a man to afflict his soul? is it to bow down his head as a bulrush, and to spread sackcloth and ashes under him? wilt thou call this a fast, and an acceptable day to the LORD?

bulwark.en: Mark ye well her bulwarks, consider her palaces; that ye may tell it to the generation following.
In that day shall this song be sung in the land of Judah; We have a strong city; salvation will God appoint for walls and bulwarks.

bunch.en: And ye shall take a bunch of hyssop, and dip it in the blood that is in the bason, and strike the lintel and the two side posts with the blood that is in the bason; and none of you shall go out at the door of his house until the morning.

And when David was a little past the top of the hill, behold, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth met him, with a couple of asses saddled, and upon them two hundred loaves of bread, and an hundred bunches of raisins, and an hundred of summer fruits, and a bottle of wine.

bundle.en: A bundle of myrrh is my well-beloved unto me; he shall lie all night betwixt my breasts.
And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid them on the fire, there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand.

burden.en: For every man shall bear his own burden.
For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.

burdensome.en: Nor of men sought we glory, neither of you, nor yet of others, when we might have been burdensome, as the apostles of Christ.
For what is it wherein ye were inferior to other churches, except it be that I myself was not burdensome to you? forgive me this wrong.

burial.en: For in that she hath poured this ointment on my body, she did it for my burial.
And devout men carried Stephen to his burial, and made great lamentation over him.

burier.en: And the passengers that pass through the land, when any seeth a man’s bone, then shall he set up a sign by it, till the buriers have buried it in the valley of Hamongog.

burn.en: And the fat of the sin offering shall he burn upon the altar.
Who is weak, and I am not weak? who is offended, and I burn not?

burned.en: Can one go upon hot coals, and his feet not be burned?
My skin is black upon me, and my bones are burned with heat.

burning.en: Burning for burning, wound for wound, stripe for stripe.
Let your loins be girded about, and your lights burning;

burnish.en: And their feet were straight feet; and the sole of their feet was like the sole of a calf’s foot: and they sparkled like the colour of burnished brass.

burnt.en: And the flesh and the hide he burnt with fire without the camp.
And he burnt sweet incense thereon; as the LORD commanded Moses.

burst.en: For now will I break his yoke from off thee, and will burst thy bonds in sunder.
Behold, my belly is as wine which hath no vent; it is ready to burst like new bottles.

bury.en: And Jair died, and was buried in Camon.
Then died Ibzan, and was buried at Bethlehem.

bush.en: Who cut up mallows by the bushes, and juniper roots for their meat.
Among the bushes they brayed; under the nettles they were gathered together.

bushel.en: And he said unto them, Is a candle brought to be put under a bushel, or under a bed? and not to be set on a candlestick?
Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel, but on a candlestick; and it giveth light unto all that are in the house.

bushy.en: His head is as the most fine gold, his locks are bushy, and black as a raven.

business.en: Not slothful in business; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord;
They that go down to the sea in ships, that do business in great waters;

busy.en: And as thy servant was busy here and there, he was gone. And the king of Israel said unto him, So shall thy judgment be; thyself hast decided it.

And afterward they made ready for themselves, and for the priests: because the priests the sons of Aaron were busied in offering of burnt offerings and the fat until night; therefore the Levites prepared for themselves, and for the priests the sons of Aaron.

busybody.en: For we hear that there are some which walk among you disorderly, working not at all, but are busybodies.
But let none of you suffer as a murderer, or as a thief, or as an evildoer, or as a busybody in other men’s matters.

butler.en: Yet did not the chief butler remember Joseph, but forgat him.
Then spake the chief butler unto Pharaoh, saying, I do remember my faults this day:

butlership.en: And he restored the chief butler unto his butlership again; and he gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hand:

butter.en: He shall not see the rivers, the floods, the brooks of honey and butter.
When I washed my steps with butter, and the rock poured me out rivers of oil;

buttock.en: Wherefore Hanun took David’s servants, and shaved them, and cut off their garments in the midst hard by their buttocks, and sent them away.
Wherefore Hanun took David’s servants, and shaved off the one half of their beards, and cut off their garments in the middle, even to their buttocks, and sent them away.

buy.en: And our father said, Go again, and buy us a little food.
And Joseph’s ten brethren went down to buy corn in Egypt.

buyer.en: It is naught, it is naught, saith the buyer: but when he is gone his way, then he boasteth.
The time is come, the day draweth near: let not the buyer rejoice, nor the seller mourn: for wrath is upon all the multitude thereof.

buz.en: Dedan, and Tema, and Buz, and all that are in the utmost corners,
Huz his firstborn, and Buz his brother, and Kemuel the father of Aram,

by.en: Give us day by day our daily bread.
(For we walk by faith, not by sight:)

byway.en: In the days of Shamgar the son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the highways were unoccupied, and the travellers walked through byways.

byword.en: And now am I their song, yea, I am their byword.
He hath made me also a byword of the people; and aforetime I was as a tabret.

cab.en: And there was a great famine in Samaria: and, behold, they besieged it, until an ass’s head was sold for fourscore pieces of silver, and the fourth part of a cab of dove’s dung for five pieces of silver.

cabin.en: When Jeremiah was entered into the dungeon, and into the cabins, and Jeremiah had remained there many days;

caesar.en: Is it lawful for us to give tribute unto Caesar, or no?
All the saints salute you, chiefly they that are of Caesar’s household.

cage.en: As a cage is full of birds, so are their houses full of deceit: therefore they are become great, and waxen rich.

And he cried mightily with a strong voice, saying, Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird.

cake.en: Ephraim, he hath mixed himself among the people; Ephraim is a cake not turned.
And thou shalt take fine flour, and bake twelve cakes thereof: two tenth deals shall be in one cake.

calamity.en: They mar my path, they set forward my calamity, they have no helper.
They prevented me in the day of my calamity: but the LORD was my stay.

calamus.en: Dan also and Javan going to and fro occupied in thy fairs: bright iron, cassia, and calamus, were in thy market.
Spikenard and saffron; calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense; myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices:

caldron.en: Out of his nostrils goeth smoke, as out of a seething pot or caldron.
Which say, It is not near; let us build houses: this city is the caldron, and we be the flesh.

calf.en: They made a calf in Horeb, and worshipped the molten image.
And bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry:

calker.en: The ancients of Gebal and the wise men thereof were in thee thy calkers: all the ships of the sea with their mariners were in thee to occupy thy merchandise.

Thy riches, and thy fairs, thy merchandise, thy mariners, and thy pilots, thy calkers, and the occupiers of thy merchandise, and all thy men of war, that are in thee, and in all thy company which is in the midst of thee, shall fall into the midst of the seas in the day of thy ruin.

call.en: For many are called, but few are chosen.
To call passengers who go right on their ways:

calling.en: For the gifts and calling of God are without repentance.
Let every man abide in the same calling wherein he was called.

calm.en: He maketh the storm a calm, so that the waves thereof are still.
And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.

calvary.en: And when they were come to the place, which is called Calvary, there they crucified him, and the malefactors, one on the right hand, and the other on the left.

calve.en: Yea, the hind also calved in the field, and forsook it, because there was no grass.
Their bull gendereth, and faileth not; their cow calveth, and casteth not her calf.

cam.en: And when they had found him on the other side of the sea, they said unto him, Rabbi, when camest thou hither?
And he saith unto him, Friend, how camest thou in hither not having a wedding garment? And he was speechless.

came.en: Of Mahli came Eleazar, who had no sons.
This day came ye out in the month Abib.

camel.en: Ye blind guides, which strain at a gnat, and swallow a camel.
Then Jacob rose up, and set his sons and his wives upon camels;

camp.en: And Moses gat him into the camp, he and the elders of Israel.
And the flesh and the hide he burnt with fire without the camp.

camphire.en: My beloved is unto me as a cluster of camphire in the vineyards of Engedi.
Thy plants are an orchard of pomegranates, with pleasant fruits; camphire, with spikenard,

can.en: Can two walk together, except they be agreed?
And they that heard it said, Who then can be saved?

canaanite.en: Simon the Canaanite, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.
And the Amorites, and the Canaanites, and the Girgashites, and the Jebusites.

canaanitish.en: And the sons of Simeon; Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanitish woman.
And the sons of Simeon; Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanitish woman: these are the families of Simeon.

candle.en: For thou wilt light my candle: the LORD my God will enlighten my darkness.
She perceiveth that her merchandise is good: her candle goeth not out by night.

candlestick.en: He shall order the lamps upon the pure candlestick before the LORD continually.
And in the candlestick were four bowls made like almonds, his knops, and his flowers:

cane.en: To what purpose cometh there to me incense from Sheba, and the sweet cane from a far country? your burnt offerings are not acceptable, nor your sacrifices sweet unto me.
Thou hast bought me no sweet cane with money, neither hast thou filled me with the fat of thy sacrifices: but thou hast made me to serve with thy sins, thou hast wearied me with thine iniquities.

canker.en: And their word will eat as doth a canker: of whom is Hymenaeus and Philetus;

cankered.en: Your gold and silver is cankered; and the rust of them shall be a witness against you, and shall eat your flesh as it were fire. Ye have heaped treasure together for the last days.

cankerworm.en: Thou hast multiplied thy merchants above the stars of heaven: the cankerworm spoileth, and fleeth away.
And I will restore to you the years that the locust hath eaten, the cankerworm, and the caterpiller, and the palmerworm, my great army which I sent among you.

cannot.en: Behold, ye trust in lying words, that cannot profit.
So then they that are in the flesh cannot please God.

captain.en: Then the band and the captain and officers of the Jews took Jesus, and bound him,
And they said one to another, Let us make a captain, and let us return into Egypt.

captive.en: He made them also to be pitied of all those that carried them captives.
Shall the prey be taken from the mighty, or the lawful captive delivered?

captivity.en: Turn again our captivity, O LORD, as the streams in the south.
And delivered his strength into captivity, and his glory into the enemy’s hand.

car.en: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.
The hireling fleeth, because he is an hireling, and careth not for the sheep.

carbuncle.en: And I will make thy windows of agates, and thy gates of carbuncles, and all thy borders of pleasant stones.
And they set in it four rows of stones: the first row was a sardius, a topaz, and a carbuncle: this was the first row.

carcase.en: But as for you, your carcases, they shall fall in this wilderness.
And when the fowls came down upon the carcases, Abram drove them away.

care.en: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.
For I have no man likeminded, who will naturally care for your state.

careful.en: And Jesus answered and said unto her, Martha, Martha, thou art careful and troubled about many things:
Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God.

carefully.en: For the inhabitant of Maroth waited carefully for good: but evil came down from the LORD unto the gate of Jerusalem.
I sent him therefore the more carefully, that, when ye see him again, ye may rejoice, and that I may be the less sorrowful.

carefulness.en: Son of man, eat thy bread with quaking, and drink thy water with trembling and with carefulness;
But I would have you without carefulness. He that is unmarried careth for the things that belong to the Lord, how he may please the Lord:

careless.en: Rise up, ye women that are at ease; hear my voice, ye careless daughters; give ear unto my speech.
Many days and years shall ye be troubled, ye careless women: for the vintage shall fail, the gathering shall not come.

carelessly.en: And I will send a fire on Magog, and among them that dwell carelessly in the isles: and they shall know that I am the LORD.

Therefore hear now this, thou that art given to pleasures, that dwellest carelessly, that sayest in thine heart, I am, and none else beside me; I shall not sit as a widow, neither shall I know the loss of children:

carmelite.en: Hezrai the Carmelite, Paarai the Arbite,
Hezro the Carmelite, Naarai the son of Ezbai,

carnal.en: For we know that the law is spiritual: but I am carnal, sold under sin.
For while one saith, I am of Paul; and another, I am of Apollos; are ye not carnal?

carnally.en: For to be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace.
Moreover thou shalt not lie carnally with thy neighbour’s wife, to defile thyself with her.

carpenter.en: And the LORD shewed me four carpenters.
Unto carpenters, and builders, and masons, and to buy timber and hewn stone to repair the house.

carpus.en: The cloke that I left at Troas with Carpus, when thou comest, bring with thee, and the books, but especially the parchments.

carriage.en: And after those days we took up our carriages, and went up to Jerusalem.
He is come to Aiath, he is passed to Migron; at Michmash he hath laid up his carriages:

carry.en: Dig thou through the wall in their sight, and carry out thereby.
Why doth thine heart carry thee away? and what do thy eyes wink at,

carrying.en: The children of Ephraim, being armed, and carrying bows, turned back in the day of battle.
Then fell she down straightway at his feet, and yielded up the ghost: and the young men came in, and found her dead, and, carrying her forth, buried her by her husband.

cart.en: Behold, I am pressed under you, as a cart is pressed that is full of sheaves.
Woe unto them that draw iniquity with cords of vanity, and sin as it were with a cart rope:

carve.en: But now they break down the carved work thereof at once with axes and hammers.
I have decked my bed with coverings of tapestry, with carved works, with fine linen of Egypt.

carving.en: And in cutting of stones, to set them, and in carving of timber, to work in all manner of workmanship.
And in the cutting of stones, to set them, and in carving of wood, to make any manner of cunning work.

case.en: Happy is that people, that is in such a case: yea, happy is that people, whose God is the LORD.
His disciples say unto him, If the case of the man be so with his wife, it is not good to marry.

casement.en: For at the window of my house I looked through my casement,

cassia.en: And of cassia five hundred shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary, and of oil olive an hin:
Dan also and Javan going to and fro occupied in thy fairs: bright iron, cassia, and calamus, were in thy market.

cast.en: For John was not yet cast into prison.
For the LORD will not cast off for ever:

castaway.en: But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway.

casting.en: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.
And he, casting away his garment, rose, and came to Jesus.

castle.en: And David dwelt in the castle; therefore they called it the city of David.
On the morrow they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the castle:

castor.en: And after three months we departed in a ship of Alexandria, which had wintered in the isle, whose sign was Castor and Pollux.

catch.en: Let the extortioner catch all that he hath; and let the strangers spoil his labour.
And they send unto him certain of the Pharisees and of the Herodians, to catch him in his words.

cattle.en: Beasts, and all cattle; creeping things, and flying fowl:
And Abram was very rich in cattle, in silver, and in gold.

caught.en: And they caught him, and beat him, and sent him away empty.
Jesus saith unto them, Bring of the fish which ye have now caught.

caul.en: But the fat, and the kidneys, and the caul above the liver of the sin offering, he burnt upon the altar; as the LORD commanded Moses.
And the fat of the bullock and of the ram, the rump, and that which covereth the inwards, and the kidneys, and the caul above the liver:

cause.en: And Moses brought their cause before the LORD.
Son of man, cause Jerusalem to know her abominations,

causeless.en: As the bird by wandering, as the swallow by flying, so the curse causeless shall not come.

That this shall be no grief unto thee, nor offence of heart unto my lord, either that thou hast shed blood causeless, or that my lord hath avenged himself: but when the LORD shall have dealt well with my lord, then remember thine handmaid.

causeway.en: At Parbar westward, four at the causeway, and two at Parbar.
To Shuppim and Hosah the lot came forth westward, with the gate Shallecheth, by the causeway of the going up, ward against ward.

cave.en: But these five kings fled, and hid themselves in a cave at Makkedah.
To dwell in the cliffs of the valleys, in caves of the earth, and in the rocks.

cease.en: Labour not to be rich: cease from thine own wisdom.

cedar.en: Mountains, and all hills; fruitful trees, and all cedars:
The beams of our house are cedar, and our rafters of fir.

ceiling.en: And he built the walls of the house within with boards of cedar, both the floor of the house, and the walls of the ceiling: and he covered them on the inside with wood, and covered the floor of the house with planks of fir.

celebrate.en: For the grave cannot praise thee, death can not celebrate thee: they that go down into the pit cannot hope for thy truth.
And ye shall keep it a feast unto the LORD seven days in the year. It shall be a statute for ever in your generations: ye shall celebrate it in the seventh month.

celestial.en: There are also celestial bodies, and bodies terrestrial: but the glory of the celestial is one, and the glory of the terrestrial is another.

cellar.en: And over the vineyards was Shimei the Ramathite: over the increase of the vineyards for the wine cellars was Zabdi the Shiphmite:
And over the olive trees and the sycomore trees that were in the low plains was Baalhanan the Gederite: and over the cellars of oil was Joash:

censer.en: This do; Take you censers, Korah, and all his company;
Speak unto Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest, that he take up the censers out of the burning, and scatter thou the fire yonder; for they are hallowed.

centurion.en: And when he knew it of the centurion, he gave the body to Joseph.
And a certain centurion’s servant, who was dear unto him, was sick, and ready to die.

certain.en: And he said, A certain man had two sons:
Howbeit we must be cast upon a certain island.

certainly.en: It is a trespass offering: he hath certainly trespassed against the LORD.
Now when the centurion saw what was done, he glorified God, saying, Certainly this was a righteous man.

certainty.en: That thou mightest know the certainty of those things, wherein thou hast been instructed.
The king answered and said, I know of certainty that ye would gain the time, because ye see the thing is gone from me.

certify.en: But I certify you, brethren, that the gospel which was preached of me is not after man.
See, I will tarry in the plain of the wilderness, until there come word from you to certify me.

chafe.en: For, said Hushai, thou knowest thy father and his men, that they be mighty men, and they be chafed in their minds, as a bear robbed of her whelps in the field: and thy father is a man of war, and will not lodge with the people.

chaff.en: The ungodly are not so: but are like the chaff which the wind driveth away.
They are as stubble before the wind, and as chaff that the storm carrieth away.

chain.en: The chains, and the bracelets, and the mufflers,
To bind their kings with chains, and their nobles with fetters of iron;
