chalcedony.en: And the foundations of the wall of the city were garnished with all manner of precious stones. The first foundation was jasper; the second, sapphire; the third, a chalcedony; the fourth, an emerald;

chaldean.en: In that night was Belshazzar the king of the Chaldeans slain.
Wherefore at that time certain Chaldeans came near, and accused the Jews.

chaldee.en: And Haran died before his father Terah in the land of his nativity, in Ur of the Chaldees.
And he said unto him, I am the LORD that brought thee out of Ur of the Chaldees, to give thee this land to inherit it.

chalkstone.en: By this therefore shall the iniquity of Jacob be purged; and this is all the fruit to take away his sin; when he maketh all the stones of the altar as chalkstones that are beaten in sunder, the groves and images shall not stand up.

challenge.en: For all manner of trespass, whether it be for ox, for ass, for sheep, for raiment, or for any manner of lost thing, which another challengeth to be his, the cause of both parties shall come before the judges; and whom the judges shall condemn, he shall pay double unto his neighbour.

chamber.en: Her house is the way to hell, going down to the chambers of death.
Which maketh Arcturus, Orion, and Pleiades, and the chambers of the south.

chambering.en: Let us walk honestly, as in the day; not in rioting and drunkenness, not in chambering and wantonness, not in strife and envying.

chamberlain.en: Gaius mine host, and of the whole church, saluteth you. Erastus the chamberlain of the city saluteth you, and Quartus a brother.
And while they were yet talking with him, came the king’s chamberlains, and hasted to bring Haman unto the banquet that Esther had prepared.

chameleon.en: And the ferret, and the chameleon, and the lizard, and the snail, and the mole.

chamois.en: The hart, and the roebuck, and the fallow deer, and the wild goat, and the pygarg, and the wild ox, and the chamois.

champaign.en: Are they not on the other side Jordan, by the way where the sun goeth down, in the land of the Canaanites, which dwell in the champaign over against Gilgal, beside the plains of Moreh?

champion.en: And there went out a champion out of the camp of the Philistines, named Goliath, of Gath, whose height was six cubits and a span.

And as he talked with them, behold, there came up the champion, the Philistine of Gath, Goliath by name, out of the armies of the Philistines, and spake according to the same words: and David heard them.

chance.en: And by chance there came down a certain priest that way: and when he saw him, he passed by on the other side.
And that which thou sowest, thou sowest not that body that shall be, but bare grain, it may chance of wheat, or of some other grain:

chancellor.en: Rehum the chancellor and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter against Jerusalem to Artaxerxes the king in this sort:

Then sent the king an answer unto Rehum the chancellor, and to Shimshai the scribe, and to the rest of their companions that dwell in Samaria, and unto the rest beyond the river, Peace, and at such a time.

change.en: They change the night into day: the light is short because of darkness.
For I am the LORD, I change not; therefore ye sons of Jacob are not consumed.

changeable.en: The changeable suits of apparel, and the mantles, and the wimples, and the crisping pins,

changer.en: And found in the temple those that sold oxen and sheep and doves, and the changers of money sitting:
And when he had made a scourge of small cords, he drove them all out of the temple, and the sheep, and the oxen; and poured out the changers’ money, and overthrew the tables;

channel.en: Then the channels of waters were seen, and the foundations of the world were discovered at thy rebuke, O LORD, at the blast of the breath of thy nostrils.
And the channels of the sea appeared, the foundations of the world were discovered, at the rebuking of the LORD, at the blast of the breath of his nostrils.

chant.en: That chant to the sound of the viol, and invent to themselves instruments of musick, like David;

chapel.en: But prophesy not again any more at Bethel: for it is the king’s chapel, and it is the king’s court.

chapiter.en: And the chapiters that were upon the top of the pillars were of lily work in the porch, four cubits.
And of the thousand seven hundred seventy and five shekels he made hooks for the pillars, and overlaid their chapiters, and filleted them.

charge.en: And I charged Baruch before them, saying,
And Moses charged the people the same day, saying,

chargeable.en: Neither did we eat any man’s bread for nought; but wrought with labour and travail night and day, that we might not be chargeable to any of you:
And the king said to Absalom, Nay, my son, let us not all now go, lest we be chargeable unto thee. And he pressed him: howbeit he would not go, but blessed him.

charger.en: And his head was brought in a charger, and given to the damsel: and she brought it to her mother.
And brought his head in a charger, and gave it to the damsel: and the damsel gave it to her mother.

chariot.en: Dedan was thy merchant in precious clothes for chariots.
King Solomon made himself a chariot of the wood of Lebanon.

charitably.en: But if thy brother be grieved with thy meat, now walkest thou not charitably. Destroy not him with thy meat, for whom Christ died.

charity.en: Let all your things be done with charity.
And to godliness brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness charity.

charm.en: For, behold, I will send serpents, cockatrices, among you, which will not be charmed, and they shall bite you, saith the LORD.

charmer.en: Which will not hearken to the voice of charmers, charming never so wisely.
Or a charmer, or a consulter with familiar spirits, or a wizard, or a necromancer.

charming.en: Which will not hearken to the voice of charmers, charming never so wisely.

chase.en: Mine enemies chased me sore, like a bird, without cause.
He shall be driven from light into darkness, and chased out of the world.

chasing.en: And the children of Israel returned from chasing after the Philistines, and they spoiled their tents.

chaste.en: While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear.
To be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed.

chasten.en: As many as I love, I rebuke and chasten: be zealous therefore, and repent.
O LORD, rebuke me not in thy wrath: neither chasten me in thy hot displeasure.

chastened.en: For all the day long have I been plagued, and chastened every morning.
When I wept, and chastened my soul with fasting, that was to my reproach.

chastise.en: I will therefore chastise him, and release him.
And the elders of that city shall take that man and chastise him;

chastisement.en: Surely it is meet to be said unto God, I have borne chastisement, I will not offend any more:
But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.

chatter.en: Like a crane or a swallow, so did I chatter: I did mourn as a dove: mine eyes fail with looking upward: O LORD, I am oppressed; undertake for me.

check.en: I have heard the check of my reproach, and the spirit of my understanding causeth me to answer.

checker.en: And nets of checker work, and wreaths of chain work, for the chapiters which were upon the top of the pillars; seven for the one chapiter, and seven for the other chapiter.

cheek.en: Thy cheeks are comely with rows of jewels, thy neck with chains of gold.
He giveth his cheek to him that smiteth him: he is filled full with reproach.

cheer.en: Then were they all of good cheer, and they also took some meat.
But straightway Jesus spake unto them, saying, Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.

cheerful.en: A merry heart maketh a cheerful countenance: but by sorrow of the heart the spirit is broken.
For how great is his goodness, and how great is his beauty! corn shall make the young men cheerful, and new wine the maids.

cheerfully.en: Then Paul, after that the governor had beckoned unto him to speak, answered, Forasmuch as I know that thou hast been of many years a judge unto this nation, I do the more cheerfully answer for myself:

cheerfulness.en: Or he that exhorteth, on exhortation: he that giveth, let him do it with simplicity; he that ruleth, with diligence; he that sheweth mercy, with cheerfulness.

cheese.en: Hast thou not poured me out as milk, and curdled me like cheese?
And carry these ten cheeses unto the captain of their thousand, and look how thy brethren fare, and take their pledge.

cherish.en: But we were gentle among you, even as a nurse cherisheth her children:
And the damsel was very fair, and cherished the king, and ministered to him: but the king knew her not.

cherub.en: The height of the one cherub was ten cubits, and so was it of the other cherub.
And he rode upon a cherub, and did fly: and he was seen upon the wings of the wind.

cherubim.en: And he overlaid the cherubims with gold.
And there appeared in the cherubims the form of a man’s hand under their wings.

ches.en: And Chesed, and Hazo, and Pildash, and Jidlaph, and Bethuel.

chest.en: And at the king’s commandment they made a chest, and set it without at the gate of the house of the LORD.
And all the princes and all the people rejoiced, and brought in, and cast into the chest, until they had made an end.

chestnut.en: And Jacob took him rods of green poplar, and of the hazel and chestnut tree; and pilled white strakes in them, and made the white appear which was in the rods.

The cedars in the garden of God could not hide him: the fir trees were not like his boughs, and the chestnut trees were not like his branches; nor any tree in the garden of God was like unto him in his beauty.

chew.en: And the hare, because he cheweth the cud, but divideth not the hoof; he is unclean unto you.
And the coney, because he cheweth the cud, but divideth not the hoof; he is unclean unto you.

chicken.en: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!

chide.en: He will not always chide: neither will he keep his anger for ever.
Wherefore the people did chide with Moses, and said, Give us water that we may drink. And Moses said unto them, Why chide ye with me? wherefore do ye tempt the LORD?

chief.en: Of the sons of Izhar; Shelomith the chief.
Of the sons of Gershom, Shebuel was the chief.

chiefest.en: My beloved is white and ruddy, the chiefest among ten thousand.
For I suppose I was not a whit behind the very chiefest apostles.

chiefly.en: All the saints salute you, chiefly they that are of Caesar’s household.
Much every way: chiefly, because that unto them were committed the oracles of God.

child.en: But Sarai was barren; she had no child.
Ye shall not afflict any widow, or fatherless child.

childbearing.en: Notwithstanding she shall be saved in childbearing, if they continue in faith and charity and holiness with sobriety.

childhood.en: Therefore remove sorrow from thy heart, and put away evil from thy flesh: for childhood and youth are vanity.
And now, behold, the king walketh before you: and I am old and grayheaded; and, behold, my sons are with you: and I have walked before you from my childhood unto this day.

childish.en: When I was a child, I spake as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child: but when I became a man, I put away childish things.

children.en: The children of Nebo, fifty and two.
The children of Gibbar, ninety and five.

chimney.en: Therefore they shall be as the morning cloud, and as the early dew that passeth away, as the chaff that is driven with the whirlwind out of the floor, and as the smoke out of the chimney.

chisleu.en: The words of Nehemiah the son of Hachaliah. And it came to pass in the month Chisleu, in the twentieth year, as I was in Shushan the palace,
And it came to pass in the fourth year of king Darius, that the word of the LORD came unto Zechariah in the fourth day of the ninth month, even in Chisleu;

chode.en: And the people chode with Moses, and spake, saying, Would God that we had died when our brethren died before the LORD!
And Jacob was wroth, and chode with Laban: and Jacob answered and said to Laban, What is my trespass? what is my sin, that thou hast so hotly pursued after me?

choice.en: Receive my instruction, and not silver; and knowledge rather than choice gold.
The tongue of the just is as choice silver: the heart of the wicked is little worth.

choke.en: And some fell among thorns; and the thorns sprung up, and choked them:
And some fell among thorns; and the thorns sprang up with it, and choked it.

choler.en: And the king of the south shall be moved with choler, and shall come forth and fight with him, even with the king of the north: and he shall set forth a great multitude; but the multitude shall be given into his hand.

And I saw him come close unto the ram, and he was moved with choler against him, and smote the ram, and brake his two horns: and there was no power in the ram to stand before him, but he cast him down to the ground, and stamped upon him: and there was none that could deliver the ram out of his hand.

choose.en: Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways.
So that my soul chooseth strangling, and death rather than my life.

chop.en: Who also eat the flesh of my people, and flay their skin from off them; and they break their bones, and chop them in pieces, as for the pot, and as flesh within the caldron.

chose.en: But chose the tribe of Judah, the mount Zion which he loved.
He chose David also his servant, and took him from the sheepfolds:

chosen.en: For many are called, but few are chosen.
Let thine hand help me; for I have chosen thy precepts.

christ.en: But ye have not so learned Christ;
And ye are Christ’s; and Christ is God’s.

christian.en: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian.
Yet if any man suffer as a Christian, let him not be ashamed; but let him glorify God on this behalf.

chronicle.en: And the rest of the acts of Amaziah, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
And the rest of the acts of Zachariah, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

chrysoprasus.en: The fifth, sardonyx; the sixth, sardius; the seventh, chrysolyte; the eighth, beryl; the ninth, a topaz; the tenth, a chrysoprasus; the eleventh, a jacinth; the twelfth, an amethyst.

chub.en: Ethiopia, and Libya, and Lydia, and all the mingled people, and Chub, and the men of the land that is in league, shall fall with them by the sword.

church.en: And he went through Syria and Cilicia, confirming the churches.
I robbed other churches, taking wages of them, to do you service.

churl.en: The vile person shall be no more called liberal, nor the churl said to be bountiful.
The instruments also of the churl are evil: he deviseth wicked devices to destroy the poor with lying words, even when the needy speaketh right.

churlish.en: Now the name of the man was Nabal; and the name of his wife Abigail: and she was a woman of good understanding, and of a beautiful countenance: but the man was churlish and evil in his doings; and he was of the house of Caleb.

churning.en: Surely the churning of milk bringeth forth butter, and the wringing of the nose bringeth forth blood: so the forcing of wrath bringeth forth strife.

cinnamon.en: I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.
Spikenard and saffron; calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense; myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices:

circle.en: It is he that sitteth upon the circle of the earth, and the inhabitants thereof are as grasshoppers; that stretcheth out the heavens as a curtain, and spreadeth them out as a tent to dwell in:

circuit.en: Thick clouds are a covering to him, that he seeth not; and he walketh in the circuit of heaven.
And he went from year to year in circuit to Bethel, and Gilgal, and Mizpeh, and judged Israel in all those places.

circumcise.en: In the selfsame day was Abraham circumcised, and Ishmael his son.
And in the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised.

circumcision.en: What advantage then hath the Jew? or what profit is there of circumcision?
So he let him go: then she said, A bloody husband thou art, because of the circumcision.

circumspect.en: And in all things that I have said unto you be circumspect: and make no mention of the name of other gods, neither let it be heard out of thy mouth.

circumspectly.en: See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise,

cistern.en: Drink waters out of thine own cistern, and running waters out of thine own well.
Or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern.

citizen.en: And he went and joined himself to a citizen of that country; and he sent him into his fields to feed swine.
But his citizens hated him, and sent a message after him, saying, We will not have this man to reign over us.

city.en: And there was great joy in that city.
And when even was come, he went out of the city.

clad.en: For he put on righteousness as a breastplate, and an helmet of salvation upon his head; and he put on the garments of vengeance for clothing, and was clad with zeal as a cloak.

And it came to pass at that time when Jeroboam went out of Jerusalem, that the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite found him in the way; and he had clad himself with a new garment; and they two were alone in the field:

clamorous.en: A foolish woman is clamorous: she is simple, and knoweth nothing.

clamour.en: Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice:

clap.en: Let the floods clap their hands: let the hills be joyful together
Men shall clap their hands at him, and shall hiss him out of his place.

clave.en: He clave the rocks in the wilderness, and gave them drink as out of the great depths.
And they lifted up their voice, and wept again: and Orpah kissed her mother in law; but Ruth clave unto her.

claw.en: And every beast that parteth the hoof, and cleaveth the cleft into two claws, and cheweth the cud among the beasts, that ye shall eat.

The same hour was the thing fulfilled upon Nebuchadnezzar: and he was driven from men, and did eat grass as oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of heaven, till his hairs were grown like eagles’ feathers, and his nails like birds’ claws.

clay.en: His legs of iron, his feet part of iron and part of clay.
It is turned as clay to the seal; and they stand as a garment.

clean.en: Of all clean birds ye shall eat.
But of all clean fowls ye may eat.

cleanness.en: Therefore the LORD hath recompensed me according to my righteousness; according to my cleanness in his eye sight.
The LORD rewarded me according to my righteousness: according to the cleanness of my hands hath he recompensed me.

cleanse.en: But if the scall spread much in the skin after his cleansing;
And after he is cleansed, they shall reckon unto him seven days.

clear.en: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the light shall not be clear, nor dark:
And the building of the wall of it was of jasper: and the city was pure gold, like unto clear glass.

clearer.en: And thine age shall be clearer than the noonday: thou shalt shine forth, thou shalt be as the morning.

clearing.en: The LORD is longsuffering, and of great mercy, forgiving iniquity and transgression, and by no means clearing the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation.

For behold this selfsame thing, that ye sorrowed after a godly sort, what carefulness it wrought in you, yea, what clearing of yourselves, yea, what indignation, yea, what fear, yea, what vehement desire, yea, what zeal, yea, what revenge! In all things ye have approved yourselves to be clear in this matter.

clearly.en: My words shall be of the uprightness of my heart: and my lips shall utter knowledge clearly.
After that he put his hands again upon his eyes, and made him look up: and he was restored, and saw every man clearly.

clearness.en: And they saw the God of Israel: and there was under his feet as it were a paved work of a sapphire stone, and as it were the body of heaven in his clearness.

cleave.en: But cleave unto the LORD your God, as ye have done unto this day.
By reason of the voice of my groaning my bones cleave to my skin.

cleft.en: For, behold, the LORD commandeth, and he will smite the great house with breaches, and the little house with clefts.
And every beast that parteth the hoof, and cleaveth the cleft into two claws, and cheweth the cud among the beasts, that ye shall eat.

clemency.en: Notwithstanding, that I be not further tedious unto thee, I pray thee that thou wouldest hear us of thy clemency a few words.

clement.en: And I intreat thee also, true yokefellow, help those women which laboured with me in the gospel, with Clement also, and with other my fellowlabourers, whose names are in the book of life.

cliff.en: To dwell in the cliffs of the valleys, in caves of the earth, and in the rocks.
To morrow go ye down against them: behold, they come up by the cliff of Ziz; and ye shall find them at the end of the brook, before the wilderness of Jeruel.

clift.en: Enflaming yourselves with idols under every green tree, slaying the children in the valleys under the clifts of the rocks?
And it shall come to pass, while my glory passeth by, that I will put thee in a clift of the rock, and will cover thee with my hand while I pass by:

climb.en: And he ran before, and climbed up into a sycomore tree to see him: for he was to pass that way.
Though they dig into hell, thence shall mine hand take them; though they climb up to heaven, thence will I bring them down:

cloak.en: And if any man will sue thee at the law, and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloak also.
If I had not come and spoken unto them, they had not had sin: but now they have no cloak for their sin.

clod.en: When the dust groweth into hardness, and the clods cleave fast together?
Doth the plowman plow all day to sow? doth he open and break the clods of his ground?

cloke.en: As free, and not using your liberty for a cloke of maliciousness, but as the servants of God.
For neither at any time used we flattering words, as ye know, nor a cloke of covetousness; God is witness:

close.en: His scales are his pride, shut up together as with a close seal.
The strangers shall fade away, and be afraid out of their close places.

closer.en: A man that hath friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.

closet.en: Therefore whatsoever ye have spoken in darkness shall be heard in the light; and that which ye have spoken in the ear in closets shall be proclaimed upon the housetops.
But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door, pray to thy Father which is in secret; and thy Father which seeth in secret shall reward thee openly.

cloth.en: And he left the linen cloth, and fled from them naked.
If so be that being clothed we shall not be found naked.

clothe.en: And thou shalt bring his sons, and clothe them with coats:
I clothe the heavens with blackness, and I make sackcloth their covering.

clothes.en: And as he went, they spread their clothes in the way.
Dedan was thy merchant in precious clothes for chariots.

clothing.en: The lambs are for thy clothing, and the goats are the price of the field.
She maketh herself coverings of tapestry; her clothing is silk and purple.

cloud.en: Which the clouds do drop and distil upon man abundantly.
And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea;

cloudy.en: He spake unto them in the cloudy pillar: they kept his testimonies, and the ordinance that he gave them.
For the day is near, even the day of the LORD is near, a cloudy day; it shall be the time of the heathen.

clout.en: And old shoes and clouted upon their feet, and old garments upon them; and all the bread of their provision was dry and mouldy.
And Ebedmelech the Ethiopian said unto Jeremiah, Put now these old cast clouts and rotten rags under thine armholes under the cords. And Jeremiah did so.

cloven.en: And there appeared unto them cloven tongues like as of fire, and it sat upon each of them.

Nevertheless these ye shall not eat of them that chew the cud, or of them that divide the cloven hoof; as the camel, and the hare, and the coney: for they chew the cud, but divide not the hoof; therefore they are unclean unto you.

cluster.en: My beloved is unto me as a cluster of camphire in the vineyards of Engedi.
This thy stature is like to a palm tree, and thy breasts to clusters of grapes.

coal.en: Sharp arrows of the mighty, with coals of juniper.
Can one go upon hot coals, and his feet not be burned?

coast.en: And they began to pray him to depart out of their coasts.
Thou art to pass over through Ar, the coast of Moab, this day:

coat.en: But be shod with sandals; and not put on two coats.
And thou shalt bring his sons, and put coats upon them.

cock.en: Peter then denied again: and immediately the cock crew.
Then began he to curse and to swear, saying, I know not the man. And immediately the cock crew.

cockatrice.en: And the sucking child shall play on the hole of the asp, and the weaned child shall put his hand on the cockatrice’ den.
For, behold, I will send serpents, cockatrices, among you, which will not be charmed, and they shall bite you, saith the LORD.

cockcrowing.en: Watch ye therefore: for ye know not when the master of the house cometh, at even, or at midnight, or at the cockcrowing, or in the morning:

cockle.en: Let thistles grow instead of wheat, and cockle instead of barley. The words of Job are ended.

coffer.en: And they laid the ark of the LORD upon the cart, and the coffer with the mice of gold and the images of their emerods.
And take the ark of the LORD, and lay it upon the cart; and put the jewels of gold, which ye return him for a trespass offering, in a coffer by the side thereof; and send it away, that it may go.

coffin.en: So Joseph died, being an hundred and ten years old: and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.

cogitation.en: Hitherto is the end of the matter. As for me Daniel, my cogitations much troubled me, and my countenance changed in me: but I kept the matter in my heart.

cold.en: Out of the south cometh the whirlwind: and cold out of the north.
And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold.

collar.en: By the great force of my disease is my garment changed: it bindeth me about as the collar of my coat.

And the weight of the golden earrings that he requested was a thousand and seven hundred shekels of gold; beside ornaments, and collars, and purple raiment that was on the kings of Midian, and beside the chains that were about their camels’ necks.

collection.en: Now concerning the collection for the saints, as I have given order to the churches of Galatia, even so do ye.
And they made a proclamation through Judah and Jerusalem, to bring in to the LORD the collection that Moses the servant of God laid upon Israel in the wilderness.

college.en: And Hilkiah, and they that the king had appointed, went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum the son of Tikvath, the son of Hasrah, keeper of the wardrobe; (now she dwelt in Jerusalem in the college:) and they spake to her to that effect.

So Hilkiah the priest, and Ahikam, and Achbor, and Shaphan, and Asahiah, went unto Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum the son of Tikvah, the son of Harhas, keeper of the wardrobe; (now she dwelt in Jerusalem in the college;) and they communed with her.

collop.en: Because he covereth his face with his fatness, and maketh collops of fat on his flanks.

colony.en: And from thence to Philippi, which is the chief city of that part of Macedonia, and a colony: and we were in that city abiding certain days.

colour.en: And the manna was as coriander seed, and the colour thereof as the colour of bdellium.
Look not thou upon the wine when it is red, when it giveth his colour in the cup, when it moveth itself aright.

coloured.en: So he carried me away in the spirit into the wilderness: and I saw a woman sit upon a scarlet coloured beast, full of names of blasphemy, having seven heads and ten horns.

colours.en: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age: and he made him a coat of many colours.
And Tamar put ashes on her head, and rent her garment of divers colours that was on her, and laid her hand on her head, and went on crying.

colt.en: For vain man would be wise, though man be born like a wild ass’s colt.
Fear not, daughter of Sion: behold, thy King cometh, sitting on an ass’s colt.

come.en: Do thy diligence to come shortly unto me:
And when ye come into an house, salute it.

comeliness.en: They of Persia and of Lud and of Phut were in thine army, thy men of war: they hanged the shield and helmet in thee; they set forth thy comeliness.
And thy renown went forth among the heathen for thy beauty: for it was perfect through my comeliness, which I had put upon thee, saith the Lord GOD.

comely.en: I have likened the daughter of Zion to a comely and delicate woman.
There be three things which go well, yea, four are comely in going:

comer.en: For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect.

comfort.en: Wherefore comfort one another with these words.
Comfort ye, comfort ye my people, saith your God.

comfortable.en: And the LORD answered the angel that talked with me with good words and comfortable words.
Then thine handmaid said, The word of my lord the king shall now be comfortable: for as an angel of God, so is my lord the king to discern good and bad: therefore the LORD thy God will be with thee.

comfortably.en: Therefore, behold, I will allure her, and bring her into the wilderness, and speak comfortably unto her.
And he set captains of war over the people, and gathered them together to him in the street of the gate of the city, and spake comfortably to them, saying,

comforter.en: I have heard many such things: miserable comforters are ye all.
And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever;

comfortless.en: I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you.

coming.en: Lest coming suddenly he find you sleeping.
And he was with them coming in and going out at Jerusalem.

command.en: Ye are my friends, if ye do whatsoever I command you.

commander.en: Behold, I have given him for a witness to the people, a leader and commander to the people.

commanding.en: Commanding his accusers to come unto thee: by examining of whom thyself mayest take knowledge of all these things, whereof we accuse him.
And it came to pass, when Jesus had made an end of commanding his twelve disciples, he departed thence to teach and to preach in their cities.

commandment.en: If ye love me, keep my commandments.
This is the first and great commandment.

commend.en: For not he that commendeth himself is approved, but whom the Lord commendeth.
I commend unto you Phebe our sister, which is a servant of the church which is at Cenchrea:

commendation.en: Do we begin again to commend ourselves? or need we, as some others, epistles of commendation to you, or letters of commendation from you?

commission.en: Whereupon as I went to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests,
And they delivered the king’s commissions unto the king’s lieutenants, and to the governors on this side the river: and they furthered the people, and the house of God.

committee.en: But as a wife that committeth adultery, which taketh strangers instead of her husband!
Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.

commodious.en: And because the haven was not commodious to winter in, the more part advised to depart thence also, if by any means they might attain to Phenice, and there to winter; which is an haven of Crete, and lieth toward the south west and north west.

common.en: And all that believed were together, and had all things common;
And laid their hands on the apostles, and put them in the common prison.

commonly.en: So they took the money, and did as they were taught: and this saying is commonly reported among the Jews until this day.
It is reported commonly that there is fornication among you, and such fornication as is not so much as named among the Gentiles, that one should have his father’s wife.

commonwealth.en: That at that time ye were without Christ, being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of promise, having no hope, and without God in the world:

commotion.en: But when ye shall hear of wars and commotions, be not terrified: for these things must first come to pass; but the end is not by and by.
Behold, the noise of the bruit is come, and a great commotion out of the north country, to make the cities of Judah desolate, and a den of dragons.

commune.en: And Hamor the father of Shechem went out unto Jacob to commune with him.
Stand in awe, and sin not: commune with your own heart upon your bed, and be still. Selah.

communicate.en: Notwithstanding ye have well done, that ye did communicate with my affliction.
Let him that is taught in the word communicate unto him that teacheth in all good things.

communication.en: Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners.
But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.

communion.en: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Ghost, be with you all. Amen.
The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ?

compact.en: Jerusalem is builded as a city that is compact together:

compacted.en: From whom the whole body fitly joined together and compacted by that which every joint supplieth, according to the effectual working in the measure of every part, maketh increase of the body unto the edifying of itself in love.

companion.en: I will answer thee, and thy companions with thee.
I am a brother to dragons, and a companion to owls.

company.en: This do; Take you censers, Korah, and all his company;
I wrote unto you in an epistle not to company with fornicators:

comparable.en: The precious sons of Zion, comparable to fine gold, how are they esteemed as earthen pitchers, the work of the hands of the potter!

compare.en: To whom then will ye liken God? or what likeness will ye compare unto him?
I have compared thee, O my love, to a company of horses in Pharaoh’s chariots.

comparison.en: And he said, Whereunto shall we liken the kingdom of God? or with what comparison shall we compare it?
Who is left among you that saw this house in her first glory? and how do ye see it now? is it not in your eyes in comparison of it as nothing?

compass.en: I will wash mine hands in innocency: so will I compass thine altar, O LORD:
From the wicked that oppress me, from my deadly enemies, who compass me about.

compassed.en: Ye have compassed this mountain long enough: turn you northward.
He hath builded against me, and compassed me with gall and travail.

compassing.en: And under the brim of it round about there were knops compassing it, ten in a cubit, compassing the sea round about: the knops were cast in two rows, when it was cast.
And under it was the similitude of oxen, which did compass it round about: ten in a cubit, compassing the sea round about. Two rows of oxen were cast, when it was cast.

compassion.en: And of some have compassion, making a difference:
And Saul said, Blessed be ye of the LORD; for ye have compassion on me.

compel.en: And whosoever shall compel thee to go a mile, go with him twain.
And the lord said unto the servant, Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.

complain.en: If my land cry against me, or that the furrows likewise thereof complain;
Wherefore doth a living man complain, a man for the punishment of his sins?

complainer.en: These are murmurers, complainers, walking after their own lusts; and their mouth speaketh great swelling words, having men’s persons in admiration because of advantage.

complaint.en: I poured out my complaint before him; I shewed before him my trouble.
When I say, My bed shall comfort me, my couch shall ease my complaint;

complete.en: And ye are complete in him, which is the head of all principality and power:
And ye shall count unto you from the morrow after the sabbath, from the day that ye brought the sheaf of the wave offering; seven sabbaths shall be complete:

composition.en: Upon man’s flesh shall it not be poured, neither shall ye make any other like it, after the composition of it: it is holy, and it shall be holy unto you.
And as for the perfume which thou shalt make, ye shall not make to yourselves according to the composition thereof: it shall be unto thee holy for the LORD.

compound.en: Whosoever compoundeth any like it, or whosoever putteth any of it upon a stranger, shall even be cut off from his people.
And thou shalt make it an oil of holy ointment, an ointment compound after the art of the apothecary: it shall be an holy anointing oil.

comprehend.en: And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not.
God thundereth marvellously with his voice; great things doeth he, which we cannot comprehend.

conceal.en: I will not conceal his parts, nor his power, nor his comely proportion.
A prudent man concealeth knowledge: but the heart of fools proclaimeth foolishness.

concealed.en: Then should I yet have comfort; yea, I would harden myself in sorrow: let him not spare; for I have not concealed the words of the Holy One.
I have not hid thy righteousness within my heart; I have declared thy faithfulness and thy salvation: I have not concealed thy lovingkindness and thy truth from the great congregation.

conceit.en: Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own conceit.
The rich man’s wealth is his strong city, and as an high wall in his own conceit.

conceive.en: And Bilhah conceived, and bare Jacob a son.
And Leah conceived again, and bare Jacob the sixth son.

conception.en: As for Ephraim, their glory shall fly away like a bird, from the birth, and from the womb, and from the conception.
So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife: and when he went in unto her, the LORD gave her conception, and she bare a son.

concern.en: If I must needs glory, I will glory of the things which concern mine infirmities.
The LORD will perfect that which concerneth me: thy mercy, O LORD, endureth for ever: forsake not the works of thine own hands.

concerning.en: Concerning Kish: the son of Kish was Jerahmeel.
Then Joab sent and told David all the things concerning the war;

concision.en: Beware of dogs, beware of evil workers, beware of the concision.

conclude.en: For God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all.
Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.

conclusion.en: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.

concord.en: And what concord hath Christ with Belial? or what part hath he that believeth with an infidel?

concourse.en: She crieth in the chief place of concourse, in the openings of the gates: in the city she uttereth her words, saying,
For we are in danger to be called in question for this day’s uproar, there being no cause whereby we may give an account of this concourse.

concubine.en: Maachah, Caleb’s concubine, bare Sheber, and Tirhanah.
There are threescore queens, and fourscore concubines, and virgins without number.

concupiscence.en: Not in the lust of concupiscence, even as the Gentiles which know not God:
But sin, taking occasion by the commandment, wrought in me all manner of concupiscence. For without the law sin was dead.

condemn.en: Beloved, if our heart condemn us not, then have we confidence toward God.
The LORD will not leave him in his hand, nor condemn him when he is judged.

condemnation.en: Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil.
My brethren, be not many masters, knowing that we shall receive the greater condemnation.

condemned.en: Ye have condemned and killed the just; and he doth not resist you.
When he shall be judged, let him be condemned: and let his prayer become sin.

condescend.en: Be of the same mind one toward another. Mind not high things, but condescend to men of low estate. Be not wise in your own conceits.

condition.en: Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sendeth an ambassage, and desireth conditions of peace.
And Nahash the Ammonite answered them, On this condition will I make a covenant with you, that I may thrust out all your right eyes, and lay it for a reproach upon all Israel.

conduct.en: And Barzillai the Gileadite came down from Rogelim, and went over Jordan with the king, to conduct him over Jordan.
So the king returned, and came to Jordan. And Judah came to Gilgal, to go to meet the king, to conduct the king over Jordan.

conduit.en: Then said the LORD unto Isaiah, Go forth now to meet Ahaz, thou, and Shearjashub thy son, at the end of the conduit of the upper pool in the highway of the fuller’s field;
And the king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem unto king Hezekiah with a great army. And he stood by the conduit of the upper pool in the highway of the fuller’s field.

coney.en: And the coney, because he cheweth the cud, but divideth not the hoof; he is unclean unto you.

Nevertheless these ye shall not eat of them that chew the cud, or of them that divide the cloven hoof; as the camel, and the hare, and the coney: for they chew the cud, but divide not the hoof; therefore they are unclean unto you.

confection.en: And thou shalt make it a perfume, a confection after the art of the apothecary, tempered together, pure and holy:

confederacy.en: Say ye not, A confederacy, to all them to whom this people shall say, A confederacy; neither fear ye their fear, nor be afraid.

All the men of thy confederacy have brought thee even to the border: the men that were at peace with thee have deceived thee, and prevailed against thee; they that eat thy bread have laid a wound under thee: there is none understanding in him.

confederate.en: For they have consulted together with one consent: they are confederate against thee:
And it was told the house of David, saying, Syria is confederate with Ephraim. And his heart was moved, and the heart of his people, as the trees of the wood are moved with the wind.

conference.en: But of these who seemed to be somewhat, (whatsoever they were, it maketh no matter to me: God accepteth no man’s person:) for they who seemed to be somewhat in conference added nothing to me:

confess.en: And were baptized of him in Jordan, confessing their sins.
And many that believed came, and confessed, and shewed their deeds.

confession.en: For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.
I give thee charge in the sight of God, who quickeneth all things, and before Christ Jesus, who before Pontius Pilate witnessed a good confession;

confidence.en: I rejoice therefore that I have confidence in you in all things.
It is better to trust in the LORD than to put confidence in man.

confident.en: A wise man feareth, and departeth from evil: but the fool rageth, and is confident.
And art confident that thou thyself art a guide of the blind, a light of them which are in darkness,

confidently.en: And about the space of one hour after another confidently affirmed, saying, Of a truth this fellow also was with him: for he is a Galilaean.

confirm.en: Even as the testimony of Christ was confirmed in you:
Strengthen ye the weak hands, and confirm the feeble knees.

confirmation.en: For men verily swear by the greater: and an oath for confirmation is to them an end of all strife.
Even as it is meet for me to think this of you all, because I have you in my heart; inasmuch as both in my bonds, and in the defence and confirmation of the gospel, ye all are partakers of my grace.

confiscation.en: And whosoever will not do the law of thy God, and the law of the king, let judgment be executed speedily upon him, whether it be unto death, or to banishment, or to confiscation of goods, or to imprisonment.

conflict.en: Having the same conflict which ye saw in me, and now hear to be in me.
For I would that ye knew what great conflict I have for you, and for them at Laodicea, and for as many as have not seen my face in the flesh;

conform.en: For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.
And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.

conformable.en: That I may know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, being made conformable unto his death;

confound.en: Go to, let us go down, and there confound their language, that they may not understand one another’s speech.
Thou therefore gird up thy loins, and arise, and speak unto them all that I command thee: be not dismayed at their faces, lest I confound thee before them.

confounded.en: Let them all be confounded and turned back that hate Zion.
They were confounded because they had hoped; they came thither, and were ashamed.

confus.en: For every battle of the warrior is with confused noise, and garments rolled in blood; but this shall be with burning and fuel of fire.
Some therefore cried one thing, and some another: for the assembly was confused; and the more part knew not wherefore they were come together.

confusion.en: In thee, O LORD, do I put my trust: let me never be put to confusion.
For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work.

congeal.en: And with the blast of thy nostrils the waters were gathered together, the floods stood upright as an heap, and the depths were congealed in the heart of the sea.

congratulate.en: He sent Hadoram his son to king David, to enquire of his welfare, and to congratulate him, because he had fought against Hadarezer, and smitten him; (for Hadarezer had war with Tou;) and with him all manner of vessels of gold and silver and brass.

congregation.en: All the congregation of Israel shall keep it.
And the thing pleased the king and all the congregation.

conquer.en: And I saw, and behold a white horse: and he that sat on him had a bow; and a crown was given unto him: and he went forth conquering, and to conquer.

conqueror.en: Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us.

conscience.en: Holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience.
Speaking lies in hypocrisy; having their conscience seared with a hot iron;

consecrate.en: And the consecrated things were six hundred oxen and three thousand sheep.
Seven days shall they purge the altar and purify it; and they shall consecrate themselves.

consecration.en: And thou shalt take the ram of the consecration, and seethe his flesh in the holy place.
And he brought the other ram, the ram of consecration: and Aaron and his sons laid their hands upon the head of the ram.

consent.en: My son, if sinners entice thee, consent thou not.
So he consented to them in this matter, and proved them ten days.

consider.en: Thus saith the LORD of hosts; Consider your ways.
Give ear to my words, O LORD, consider my meditation.

consist.en: And he is before all things, and by him all things consist.
And he said unto them, Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man’s life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth.

consolation.en: Which when they had read, they rejoiced for the consolation.
Hear diligently my speech, and let this be your consolations.

consort.en: And some of them believed, and consorted with Paul and Silas; and of the devout Greeks a great multitude, and of the chief women not a few.

conspiracy.en: And they were more than forty which had made this conspiracy.
And his servants arose, and made a conspiracy, and slew Joash in the house of Millo, which goeth down to Silla.

conspirator.en: And one told David, saying, Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom. And David said, O LORD, I pray thee, turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness.

conspire.en: And his servants conspired against him, and slew him in his own house.
And the servants of Amon conspired against him, and slew the king in his own house.

constant.en: Moreover I will establish his kingdom for ever, if he be constant to do my commandments and my judgments, as at this day.

constantly.en: A false witness shall perish: but the man that heareth speaketh constantly.
And they said unto her, Thou art mad. But she constantly affirmed that it was even so. Then said they, It is his angel.

constellation.en: For the stars of heaven and the constellations thereof shall not give their light: the sun shall be darkened in his going forth, and the moon shall not cause her light to shine.

constrain.en: For I am full of matter, the spirit within me constraineth me.
For the love of Christ constraineth us; because we thus judge, that if one died for all, then were all dead:

constrained.en: But when the Jews spake against it, I was constrained to appeal unto Caesar; not that I had ought to accuse my nation of.
But they constrained him, saying, Abide with us: for it is toward evening, and the day is far spent. And he went in to tarry with them.

constraint.en: Feed the flock of God which is among you, taking the oversight thereof, not by constraint, but willingly; not for filthy lucre, but of a ready mind;

consult.en: And consulted that they might take Jesus by subtilty, and kill him.
But the chief priests consulted that they might put Lazarus also to death;

consultation.en: And straightway in the morning the chief priests held a consultation with the elders and scribes and the whole council, and bound Jesus, and carried him away, and delivered him to Pilate.

consulter.en: Or a charmer, or a consulter with familiar spirits, or a wizard, or a necromancer.

consume.en: For our God is a consuming fire.
For the LORD thy God is a consuming fire, even a jealous God.

consummation.en: And he shall confirm the covenant with many for one week: and in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease, and for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate, even until the consummation, and that determined shall be poured upon the desolate.

consumption.en: For the Lord GOD of hosts shall make a consumption, even determined, in the midst of all the land.
For though thy people Israel be as the sand of the sea, yet a remnant of them shall return: the consumption decreed shall overflow with righteousness.

contain.en: But if they cannot contain, let them marry: for it is better to marry than to burn.
And there were set there six waterpots of stone, after the manner of the purifying of the Jews, containing two or three firkins apiece.

contemn.en: Wherefore doth the wicked contemn God? he hath said in his heart, Thou wilt not require it.
Because they rebelled against the words of God, and contemned the counsel of the most High:

contempt.en: Remove from me reproach and contempt; for I have kept thy testimonies.
He poureth contempt upon princes, and weakeneth the strength of the mighty.

contemptible.en: For his letters, say they, are weighty and powerful; but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech contemptible.
But ye have profaned it, in that ye say, The table of the LORD is polluted; and the fruit thereof, even his meat, is contemptible.

contemptuously.en: Let the lying lips be put to silence; which speak grievous things proudly and contemptuously against the righteous.

contend.en: Will ye accept his person? will ye contend for God?
If he will contend with him, he cannot answer him one of a thousand.

content.en: And when Moses heard that, he was content.
And having food and raiment let us be therewith content.

contention.en: Only by pride cometh contention: but with the well advised is wisdom.
The lot causeth contentions to cease, and parteth between the mighty.

contentious.en: A continual dropping in a very rainy day and a contentious woman are alike.
It is better to dwell in the wilderness, than with a contentious and an angry woman.

contentment.en: But godliness with contentment is great gain.

continual.en: That I have great heaviness and continual sorrow in my heart.
A continual dropping in a very rainy day and a contentious woman are alike.

continually.en: So shall I keep thy law continually for ever and ever.
Seek the LORD and his strength, seek his face continually.

continuance.en: To them who by patient continuance in well doing seek for glory and honour and immortality, eternal life:
Then the LORD will make thy plagues wonderful, and the plagues of thy seed, even great plagues, and of long continuance, and sore sicknesses, and of long continuance.

continue.en: Continue in prayer, and watch in the same with thanksgiving;

continued.en: Moreover Job continued his parable, and said,
Moreover Job continued his parable, and said,

contradict.en: But when the Jews saw the multitudes, they were filled with envy, and spake against those things which were spoken by Paul, contradicting and blaspheming.

contradiction.en: And without all contradiction the less is blessed of the better.
For consider him that endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, lest ye be wearied and faint in your minds.

contrariwise.en: So that contrariwise ye ought rather to forgive him, and comfort him, lest perhaps such a one should be swallowed up with overmuch sorrow.
But contrariwise, when they saw that the gospel of the uncircumcision was committed unto me, as the gospel of the circumcision was unto Peter;

contrary.en: Saying, This fellow persuadeth men to worship God contrary to the law.
And if ye will not for all this hearken unto me, but walk contrary unto me;

contribution.en: For it hath pleased them of Macedonia and Achaia to make a certain contribution for the poor saints which are at Jerusalem.

contrite.en: The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.
The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.

controversy.en: For it is the day of the LORD’s vengeance, and the year of recompences for the controversy of Zion.
The LORD hath also a controversy with Judah, and will punish Jacob according to his ways; according to his doings will he recompense him.

convenient.en: Wherefore, though I might be much bold in Christ to enjoin thee that which is convenient,
Neither filthiness, nor foolish talking, nor jesting, which are not convenient: but rather giving of thanks.

conveniently.en: And when they heard it, they were glad, and promised to give him money. And he sought how he might conveniently betray him.

conversant.en: But the men were very good unto us, and we were not hurt, neither missed we any thing, as long as we were conversant with them, when we were in the fields:
There was not a word of all that Moses commanded, which Joshua read not before all the congregation of Israel, with the women, and the little ones, and the strangers that were conversant among them.

conversation.en: While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear.
And delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked:

conversion.en: And being brought on their way by the church, they passed through Phenice and Samaria, declaring the conversion of the Gentiles: and they caused great joy unto all the brethren.

convert.en: Brethren, if any of you do err from the truth, and one convert him;
Zion shall be redeemed with judgment, and her converts with righteousness.

convey.en: And he that was healed wist not who it was: for Jesus had conveyed himself away, a multitude being in that place.
Moreover I said unto the king, If it please the king, let letters be given me to the governors beyond the river, that they may convey me over till I come into Judah;

convict.en: And they which heard it, being convicted by their own conscience, went out one by one, beginning at the eldest, even unto the last: and Jesus was left alone, and the woman standing in the midst.

convince.en: Which of you convinceth me of sin? And if I say the truth, why do ye not believe me?
But if ye have respect to persons, ye commit sin, and are convinced of the law as transgressors.

convocation.en: On the first day shall be an holy convocation: ye shall do no servile work therein.
And on the seventh day ye shall have an holy convocation; ye shall do no servile work.

coo.en: And it came to pass, that after we were gotten from them, and had launched, we came with a straight course unto Coos, and the day following unto Rhodes, and from thence unto Patara:

cook.en: And he will take your daughters to be confectionaries, and to be cooks, and to be bakers.
And Samuel said unto the cook, Bring the portion which I gave thee, of which I said unto thee, Set it by thee.

cool.en: And he cried and said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame.
And they heard the voice of the LORD God walking in the garden in the cool of the day: and Adam and his wife hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God amongst the trees of the garden.

coping.en: All these were of costly stones, according to the measures of hewed stones, sawed with saws, within and without, even from the foundation unto the coping, and so on the outside toward the great court.

copper.en: Also twenty basons of gold, of a thousand drams; and two vessels of fine copper, precious as gold.

coppersmith.en: Alexander the coppersmith did me much evil: the Lord reward him according to his works:

copulation.en: And if any man’s seed of copulation go out from him, then he shall wash all his flesh in water, and be unclean until the even.
And every garment, and every skin, whereon is the seed of copulation, shall be washed with water, and be unclean until the even.

copy.en: These are also proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.
And he wrote there upon the stones a copy of the law of Moses, which he wrote in the presence of the children of Israel.

cor.en: Concerning the ordinance of oil, the bath of oil, ye shall offer the tenth part of a bath out of the cor, which is an homer of ten baths; for ten baths are an homer:

coral.en: No mention shall be made of coral, or of pearls: for the price of wisdom is above rubies.
Syria was thy merchant by reason of the multitude of the wares of thy making: they occupied in thy fairs with emeralds, purple, and broidered work, and fine linen, and coral, and agate.

corban.en: But ye say, If a man shall say to his father or mother, It is Corban, that is to say, a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; he shall be free.

cord.en: The LORD is righteous: he hath cut asunder the cords of the wicked.
Let us break their bands asunder, and cast away their cords from us.

core.en: Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core.

coriander.en: And the manna was as coriander seed, and the colour thereof as the colour of bdellium.
And the house of Israel called the name thereof Manna: and it was like coriander seed, white; and the taste of it was like wafers made with honey.

corinth.en: After these things Paul departed from Athens, and came to Corinth;
Erastus abode at Corinth: but Trophimus have I left at Miletum sick.

corinthian.en: O ye Corinthians, our mouth is open unto you, our heart is enlarged.
And Crispus, the chief ruler of the synagogue, believed on the Lord with all his house; and many of the Corinthians hearing believed, and were baptized.

cormorant.en: And the pelican, and the gier eagle, and the cormorant,
And the little owl, and the cormorant, and the great owl,

corn.en: And Joseph’s ten brethren went down to buy corn in Egypt.
Thou shalt not muzzle the ox when he treadeth out the corn.

corner.en: Dedan, and Tema, and Buz, and all that are in the utmost corners,
And two boards made he for the corners of the tabernacle in the two sides.

cornet.en: With trumpets and sound of cornet make a joyful noise before the LORD, the King.
Blow ye the cornet in Gibeah, and the trumpet in Ramah: cry aloud at Bethaven, after thee, O Benjamin.

cornfloor.en: Rejoice not, O Israel, for joy, as other people: for thou hast gone a whoring from thy God, thou hast loved a reward upon every cornfloor.

corps.en: Then the angel of the LORD went forth, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred and fourscore and five thousand: and when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses.

The horseman lifteth up both the bright sword and the glittering spear: and there is a multitude of slain, and a great number of carcases; and there is none end of their corpses; they stumble upon their corpses:

corpse.en: And when his disciples heard of it, they came and took up his corpse, and laid it in a tomb.

correct.en: A servant will not be corrected by words: for though he understand he will not answer.
For whom the LORD loveth he correcteth; even as a father the son in whom he delighteth.

correction.en: He causeth it to come, whether for correction, or for his land, or for mercy.
My son, despise not the chastening of the LORD; neither be weary of his correction:

corrupt.en: Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners.
My wounds stink and are corrupt because of my foolishness.

corrupter.en: They are all grievous revolters, walking with slanders: they are brass and iron; they are all corrupters.

Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters: they have forsaken the LORD, they have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, they are gone away backward.

corruptible.en: For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality.
Being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever.

corruption.en: But he, whom God raised again, saw no corruption.
That he should still live for ever, and not see corruption.

corruptly.en: We have dealt very corruptly against thee, and have not kept the commandments, nor the statutes, nor the judgments, which thou commandedst thy servant Moses.
And he did that which was right in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his father Uzziah did: howbeit he entered not into the temple of the LORD. And the people did yet corruptly.

cost.en: For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it?
And king David said to Ornan, Nay; but I will verily buy it for the full price: for I will not take that which is thine for the LORD, nor offer burnt offerings without cost.

costliness.en: And they cast dust on their heads, and cried, weeping and wailing, saying, Alas, alas, that great city, wherein were made rich all that had ships in the sea by reason of her costliness! for in one hour is she made desolate.

costly.en: And above were costly stones, after the measures of hewed stones, and cedars.
And the foundation was of costly stones, even great stones, stones of ten cubits, and stones of eight cubits.

cot.en: Storehouses also for the increase of corn, and wine, and oil; and stalls for all manner of beasts, and cotes for flocks.

cottage.en: And the sea coast shall be dwellings and cottages for shepherds, and folds for flocks.
And the daughter of Zion is left as a cottage in a vineyard, as a lodge in a garden of cucumbers, as a besieged city.

couch.en: When I say, My bed shall comfort me, my couch shall ease my complaint;
When they couch in their dens, and abide in the covert to lie in wait?

couched.en: Judah is a lion’s whelp: from the prey, my son, thou art gone up: he stooped down, he couched as a lion, and as an old lion; who shall rouse him up?
He couched, he lay down as a lion, and as a great lion: who shall stir him up? Blessed is he that blesseth thee, and cursed is he that curseth thee.

couching.en: Issachar is a strong ass couching down between two burdens:
And I will make Rabbah a stable for camels, and the Ammonites a couching place for flocks: and ye shall know that I am the LORD.

could.en: If this man were not of God, he could do nothing.
And they could not answer him again to these things.

coulter.en: Yet they had a file for the mattocks, and for the coulters, and for the forks, and for the axes, and to sharpen the goads.
But all the Israelites went down to the Philistines, to sharpen every man his share, and his coulter, and his axe, and his mattock.

council.en: Then the Pharisees went out, and held a council against him, how they might destroy him.
But when they had commanded them to go aside out of the council, they conferred among themselves,

counsel.en: They would none of my counsel: they despised all my reproof.
They soon forgat his works; they waited not for his counsel:

count.en: Doth not he see my ways, and count all my steps?
I hate them with perfect hatred: I count them mine enemies.

countenance.en: Neither shalt thou countenance a poor man in his cause.
The LORD lift up his countenance upon thee, and give thee peace.

countervail.en: For we are sold, I and my people, to be destroyed, to be slain, and to perish. But if we had been sold for bondmen and bondwomen, I had held my tongue, although the enemy could not countervail the king’s damage.

country.en: As cold waters to a thirsty soul, so is good news from a far country.
For they that say such things declare plainly that they seek a country.

couple.en: While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear.
And he coupled five curtains by themselves, and six curtains by themselves.

coupling.en: Even to the artificers and builders gave they it, to buy hewn stone, and timber for couplings, and to floor the houses which the kings of Judah had destroyed.
And he made fifty loops upon the uttermost edge of the curtain in the coupling, and fifty loops made he upon the edge of the curtain which coupleth the second.

courage.en: Be of good courage, and he shall strengthen your heart, all ye that hope in the LORD.
They helped every one his neighbour; and every one said to his brother, Be of good courage.

courageous.en: And he that is courageous among the mighty shall flee away naked in that day, saith the LORD.
Be strong and courageous, be not afraid nor dismayed for the king of Assyria, nor for all the multitude that is with him: for there be more with us than with him:

courageously.en: And, behold, Amariah the chief priest is over you in all matters of the LORD; and Zebadiah the son of Ishmael, the ruler of the house of Judah, for all the king’s matters: also the Levites shall be officers before you. Deal courageously, and the LORD shall be with the good.

course.en: They fought from heaven; the stars in their courses fought against Sisera.
I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith:

court.en: All the hangings of the court round about were of fine twined linen.
The pins of the tabernacle, and the pins of the court, and their cords,

courteous.en: Finally, be ye all of one mind, having compassion one of another, love as brethren, be pitiful, be courteous:

courteously.en: And the next day we touched at Sidon. And Julius courteously entreated Paul, and gave him liberty to go unto his friends to refresh himself.
In the same quarters were possessions of the chief man of the island, whose name was Publius; who received us, and lodged us three days courteously.

cousin.en: And her neighbours and her cousins heard how the Lord had shewed great mercy upon her; and they rejoiced with her.
And, behold, thy cousin Elisabeth, she hath also conceived a son in her old age: and this is the sixth month with her, who was called barren.

covenant.en: The LORD our God made a covenant with us in Horeb.
And they were glad, and covenanted to give him money.

cover.en: Hatred stirreth up strifes: but love covereth all sins.
O earth, cover not thou my blood, and let my cry have no place.

covered.en: And Moses went up into the mount, and a cloud covered the mount.
The depths have covered them: they sank into the bottom as a stone.

covering.en: Hell is naked before him, and destruction hath no covering.
He spread a cloud for a covering; and fire to give light in the night.

covert.en: He lieth under the shady trees, in the covert of the reed, and fens.
When they couch in their dens, and abide in the covert to lie in wait?

covet.en: I have coveted no man’s silver, or gold, or apparel.
Wherefore, brethren, covet to prophesy, and forbid not to speak with tongues.

covetous.en: And the Pharisees also, who were covetous, heard all these things: and they derided him.
For the wicked boasteth of his heart’s desire, and blesseth the covetous, whom the LORD abhorreth.

covetousness.en: Incline my heart unto thy testimonies, and not to covetousness.
Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness:

cow.en: And whether it be cow or ewe, ye shall not kill it and her young both in one day.
Their bull gendereth, and faileth not; their cow calveth, and casteth not her calf.

coz.en: And Coz begat Anub, and Zobebah, and the families of Aharhel the son of Harum.

crackling.en: For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool: this also is vanity.

cracknel.en: And take with thee ten loaves, and cracknels, and a cruse of honey, and go to him: he shall tell thee what shall become of the child.

craft.en: And because he was of the same craft, he abode with them, and wrought: for by their occupation they were tentmakers.
Whom he called together with the workmen of like occupation, and said, Sirs, ye know that by this craft we have our wealth.

craftiness.en: But he perceived their craftiness, and said unto them, Why tempt ye me?
He taketh the wise in their own craftiness: and the counsel of the froward is carried headlong.

craftsman.en: Cursed be the man that maketh any graven or molten image, an abomination unto the LORD, the work of the hands of the craftsman, and putteth it in a secret place. And all the people shall answer and say, Amen.

And the voice of harpers, and musicians, and of pipers, and trumpeters, shall be heard no more at all in thee; and no craftsman, of whatsoever craft he be, shall be found any more in thee; and the sound of a millstone shall be heard no more at all in thee;

crafty.en: For thy mouth uttereth thine iniquity, and thou choosest the tongue of the crafty.
But be it so, I did not burden you: nevertheless, being crafty, I caught you with guile.

crag.en: She dwelleth and abideth on the rock, upon the crag of the rock, and the strong place.

crane.en: Like a crane or a swallow, so did I chatter: I did mourn as a dove: mine eyes fail with looking upward: O LORD, I am oppressed; undertake for me.
Yea, the stork in the heaven knoweth her appointed times; and the turtle and the crane and the swallow observe the time of their coming; but my people know not the judgment of the LORD.

crashing.en: And it shall come to pass in that day, saith the LORD, that there shall be the noise of a cry from the fish gate, and an howling from the second, and a great crashing from the hills.

crave.en: He that laboureth laboureth for himself; for his mouth craveth it of him.
Joseph of Arimathaea, an honourable counsellor, which also waited for the kingdom of God, came, and went in boldly unto Pilate, and craved the body of Jesus.

creat.en: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
Neither was the man created for the woman; but the woman for the man.

create.en: Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.
I form the light, and create darkness: I make peace, and create evil: I the LORD do all these things.

creation.en: But from the beginning of the creation God made them male and female.
For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now.

creator.en: I am the LORD, your Holy One, the creator of Israel, your King.
Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.

creature.en: Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature:
And the living creatures ran and returned as the appearance of a flash of lightning.

creditor.en: There was a certain creditor which had two debtors: the one owed five hundred pence, and the other fifty.

And this is the manner of the release: Every creditor that lendeth ought unto his neighbour shall release it; he shall not exact it of his neighbour, or of his brother; because it is called the LORD’s release.

creek.en: And when it was day, they knew not the land: but they discovered a certain creek with a shore, into the which they were minded, if it were possible, to thrust in the ship.

creep.en: All fowls that creep, going upon all four, shall be an abomination unto you.
Thou makest darkness, and it is night: wherein all the beasts of the forest do creep forth.

creeping.en: Beasts, and all cattle; creeping things, and flying fowl:
And every creeping thing that flieth is unclean unto you: they shall not be eaten.

crept.en: For there are certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation, ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into lasciviousness, and denying the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ.

crete.en: Cretes and Arabians, we do hear them speak in our tongues the wonderful works of God.
And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, loosing thence, they sailed close by Crete.

cretian.en: One of themselves, even a prophet of their own, said, The Cretians are alway liars, evil beasts, slow bellies.

crew.en: Peter then denied again: and immediately the cock crew.
Then began he to curse and to swear, saying, I know not the man. And immediately the cock crew.

crib.en: Will the unicorn be willing to serve thee, or abide by thy crib?
Where no oxen are, the crib is clean: but much increase is by the strength of the ox.

cried.en: And they cried out again, Crucify him.
But they cried, saying, Crucify him, crucify him.

crime.en: For this is an heinous crime; yea, it is an iniquity to be punished by the judges.
Make a chain: for the land is full of bloody crimes, and the city is full of violence.

crimson.en: And he made the vail of blue, and purple, and crimson, and fine linen, and wrought cherubims thereon.
Come now, and let us reason together, saith the LORD: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.

cripple.en: And there sat a certain man at Lystra, impotent in his feet, being a cripple from his mother’s womb, who never had walked:

crisp.en: The changeable suits of apparel, and the mantles, and the wimples, and the crisping pins,

crooked.en: Whose ways are crooked, and they froward in their paths:
He hath inclosed my ways with hewn stone, he hath made my paths crooked.

crop.en: And he shall pluck away his crop with his feathers, and cast it beside the altar on the east part, by the place of the ashes:

Thus saith the Lord GOD; I will also take of the highest branch of the high cedar, and will set it; I will crop off from the top of his young twigs a tender one, and will plant it upon an high mountain and eminent:

cross.en: Save thyself, and come down from the cross.
And he that taketh not his cross, and followeth after me, is not worthy of me.

crossway.en: Neither shouldest thou have stood in the crossway, to cut off those of his that did escape; neither shouldest thou have delivered up those of his that did remain in the day of distress.

crouch.en: He croucheth, and humbleth himself, that the poor may fall by his strong ones.

And it shall come to pass, that every one that is left in thine house shall come and crouch to him for a piece of silver and a morsel of bread, and shall say, Put me, I pray thee, into one of the priests’ offices, that I may eat a piece of bread.

crow.en: Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, That this night, before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice.
And he said, I tell thee, Peter, the cock shall not crow this day, before that thou shalt thrice deny that thou knowest me.

crown.en: He hath stripped me of my glory, and taken the crown from my head.
The crown is fallen from our head: woe unto us, that we have sinned!

crowned.en: The simple inherit folly: but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.
And if a man also strive for masteries, yet is he not crowned, except he strive lawfully.

crucify.en: And they cried out again, Crucify him.
But they cried, saying, Crucify him, crucify him.

cruel.en: Their wine is the poison of dragons, and the cruel venom of asps.
Lest thou give thine honour unto others, and thy years unto the cruel:

cruelly.en: As for his father, because he cruelly oppressed, spoiled his brother by violence, and did that which is not good among his people, lo, even he shall die in his iniquity.

cruelty.en: Simeon and Levi are brethren; instruments of cruelty are in their habitations.
Have respect unto the covenant: for the dark places of the earth are full of the habitations of cruelty.

crumb.en: And she said, Truth, Lord: yet the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters’ table.
And she answered and said unto him, Yes, Lord: yet the dogs under the table eat of the children’s crumbs.

cruse.en: And he said, Bring me a new cruse, and put salt therein. And they brought it to him.
And the barrel of meal wasted not, neither did the cruse of oil fail, according to the word of the LORD, which he spake by Elijah.

crush.en: To crush under his feet all the prisoners of the earth,
And forgetteth that the foot may crush them, or that the wild beast may break them.

cry.en: Hear my cry, O God; attend unto my prayer.
Israel shall cry unto me, My God, we know thee.

crying.en: For the multitude of the people followed after, crying, Away with him.
A voice of crying shall be from Horonaim, spoiling and great destruction.

crystal.en: The gold and the crystal cannot equal it: and the exchange of it shall not be for jewels of fine gold.
And he shewed me a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb.

cubit.en: And for the east side eastward fifty cubits.
Which of you by taking thought can add one cubit unto his stature?

cucumber.en: And the daughter of Zion is left as a cottage in a vineyard, as a lodge in a garden of cucumbers, as a besieged city.
