And when he had set the brands on fire, he let them go into the standing corn of the Philistines, and burnt up both the shocks, and also the standing corn, with the vineyards and olives.

shod.en: But be shod with sandals; and not put on two coats.
And your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace;

shoe.en: Carry neither purse, nor scrip, nor shoes: and salute no man by the way.
Thy shoes shall be iron and brass; and as thy days, so shall thy strength be.

shone.en: And, lo, the angel of the Lord came upon them, and the glory of the Lord shone round about them: and they were sore afraid.
And when Aaron and all the children of Israel saw Moses, behold, the skin of his face shone; and they were afraid to come nigh him.

shook.en: And he shook off the beast into the fire, and felt no harm.
But they shook off the dust of their feet against them, and came unto Iconium.

shoot.en: He is green before the sun, and his branch shooteth forth in his garden.
But God shall shoot at them with an arrow; suddenly shall they be wounded.

shooter.en: And the shooters shot from off the wall upon thy servants; and some of the king’s servants be dead, and thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.

shooting.en: They were armed with bows, and could use both the right hand and the left in hurling stones and shooting arrows out of a bow, even of Saul’s brethren of Benjamin.
Thus hath the Lord GOD shewed unto me; and, behold, he formed grasshoppers in the beginning of the shooting up of the latter growth; and, lo, it was the latter growth after the king’s mowings.

shore.en: And when they had passed over, they came into the land of Gennesaret, and drew to the shore.
And their south border was from the shore of the salt sea, from the bay that looketh southward:

shorn.en: For if the woman be not covered, let her also be shorn: but if it be a shame for a woman to be shorn or shaven, let her be covered.
Thy teeth are like a flock of sheep that are even shorn, which came up from the washing; whereof every one bear twins, and none is barren among them.

short.en: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God;
They change the night into day: the light is short because of darkness.

shorten.en: He weakened my strength in the way; he shortened my days.
The days of his youth hast thou shortened: thou hast covered him with shame. Selah.

shortly.en: Do thy diligence to come shortly unto me:
But I trust in the Lord that I also myself shall come shortly.

shot.en: The archers have sorely grieved him, and shot at him, and hated him:
And I will shoot three arrows on the side thereof, as though I shot at a mark.

should.en: Not of works, lest any man should boast.
That no flesh should glory in his presence.

shoulder.en: And when he hath found it, he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
Surely I would take it upon my shoulder, and bind it as a crown to me.

shout.en: Also when I cry and shout, he shutteth out my prayer.
God is gone up with a shout, the LORD with the sound of a trumpet.

shovel.en: And the pots, and the shovels, and the snuffers, and the spoons, and all the vessels of brass wherewith they ministered, took they away.
The oxen likewise and the young asses that ear the ground shall eat clean provender, which hath been winnowed with the shovel and with the fan.

shower.en: He shall come down like rain upon the mown grass: as showers that water the earth.
They are wet with the showers of the mountains, and embrace the rock for want of a shelter.

shrank.en: Therefore the children of Israel eat not of the sinew which shrank, which is upon the hollow of the thigh, unto this day: because he touched the hollow of Jacob’s thigh in the sinew that shrank.

shred.en: And one went out into the field to gather herbs, and found a wild vine, and gathered thereof wild gourds his lap full, and came and shred them into the pot of pottage: for they knew them not.

shrine.en: For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, which made silver shrines for Diana, brought no small gain unto the craftsmen;

shroud.en: Behold, the Assyrian was a cedar in Lebanon with fair branches, and with a shadowing shroud, and of an high stature; and his top was among the thick boughs.

shrub.en: And the water was spent in the bottle, and she cast the child under one of the shrubs.

shun.en: But shun profane and vain babblings: for they will increase unto more ungodliness.

shut.en: Added yet this above all, that he shut up John in prison.
His scales are his pride, shut up together as with a close seal.

shuttle.en: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, and are spent without hope.

sick.en: At that time Abijah the son of Jeroboam fell sick.
Or when saw we thee sick, or in prison, and came unto thee?

sickle.en: And he that sat on the cloud thrust in his sickle on the earth; and the earth was reaped.
And another angel came out of the temple which is in heaven, he also having a sharp sickle.

sickly.en: For this cause many are weak and sickly among you, and many sleep.

sickness.en: And to have power to heal sicknesses, and to cast out devils:
All his days also he eateth in darkness, and he hath much sorrow and wrath with his sickness.

side.en: And for the east side eastward fifty cubits.
The wicked walk on every side, when the vilest men are exalted.

siege.en: Thus saith Sennacherib king of Assyria, Whereon do ye trust, that ye abide in the siege in Jerusalem?
Draw thee waters for the siege, fortify thy strong holds: go into clay, and tread the morter, make strong the brickkiln.

sieve.en: For, lo, I will command, and I will sift the house of Israel among all nations, like as corn is sifted in a sieve, yet shall not the least grain fall upon the earth.

And his breath, as an overflowing stream, shall reach to the midst of the neck, to sift the nations with the sieve of vanity: and there shall be a bridle in the jaws of the people, causing them to err.

sift.en: And the Lord said, Simon, Simon, behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat:
For, lo, I will command, and I will sift the house of Israel among all nations, like as corn is sifted in a sieve, yet shall not the least grain fall upon the earth.

sigh.en: The new wine mourneth, the vine languisheth, all the merryhearted do sigh.
And looking up to heaven, he sighed, and saith unto him, Ephphatha, that is, Be opened.

sighing.en: For my sighing cometh before I eat, and my roarings are poured out like the waters.
Thou didst say, Woe is me now! for the LORD hath added grief to my sorrow; I fainted in my sighing, and I find no rest.

sight.en: (For we walk by faith, not by sight:)
Even so, Father: for so it seemed good in thy sight.

sign.en: Wherefore king Darius signed the writing and the decree.
And others, tempting him, sought of him a sign from heaven.

signet.en: And thou shalt make a plate of pure gold, and grave upon it, like the engravings of a signet, HOLINESS TO THE LORD.
And they wrought onyx stones inclosed in ouches of gold, graven, as signets are graven, with the names of the children of Israel.

signification.en: There are, it may be, so many kinds of voices in the world, and none of them is without signification.

signify.en: This he said, signifying what death he should die.
That the saying of Jesus might be fulfilled, which he spake, signifying what death he should die.

silence.en: Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection.
Unto me men gave ear, and waited, and kept silence at my counsel.

silent.en: Be silent, O all flesh, before the LORD: for he is raised up out of his holy habitation.
O my God, I cry in the day time, but thou hearest not; and in the night season, and am not silent.

silk.en: She maketh herself coverings of tapestry; her clothing is silk and purple.
I clothed thee also with broidered work, and shod thee with badgers’ skin, and I girded thee about with fine linen, and I covered thee with silk.

silly.en: For wrath killeth the foolish man, and envy slayeth the silly one.
Ephraim also is like a silly dove without heart: they call to Egypt, they go to Assyria.

silver.en: I have coveted no man’s silver, or gold, or apparel.
Thy silver is become dross, thy wine mixed with water:

silverling.en: And it shall come to pass in that day, that every place shall be, where there were a thousand vines at a thousand silverlings, it shall even be for briers and thorns.

silversmith.en: For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, which made silver shrines for Diana, brought no small gain unto the craftsmen;

similitude.en: Thus they changed their glory into the similitude of an ox that eateth grass.
And it is yet far more evident: for that after the similitude of Melchisedec there ariseth another priest,

simple.en: A foolish woman is clamorous: she is simple, and knoweth nothing.
The LORD preserveth the simple: I was brought low, and he helped me.

simplicity.en: How long, ye simple ones, will ye love simplicity? and the scorners delight in their scorning, and fools hate knowledge?
And with Absalom went two hundred men out of Jerusalem, that were called; and they went in their simplicity, and they knew not any thing.

sin.en: For he that is dead is freed from sin.
Of sin, because they believe not on me;

since.en: Knowest thou not this of old, since man was placed upon earth,
For since by man came death, by man came also the resurrection of the dead.

sincere.en: As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby:
That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere and without offence till the day of Christ;

sincerely.en: The one preach Christ of contention, not sincerely, supposing to add affliction to my bonds:
If ye then have dealt truly and sincerely with Jerubbaal and with his house this day, then rejoice ye in Abimelech, and let him also rejoice in you:

sincerity.en: Grace be with all them that love our Lord Jesus Christ in sincerity. Amen.
In all things shewing thyself a pattern of good works: in doctrine shewing uncorruptness, gravity, sincerity,

sinew.en: My bones are pierced in me in the night season: and my sinews take no rest.
He moveth his tail like a cedar: the sinews of his stones are wrapped together.

sinful.en: When Simon Peter saw it, he fell down at Jesus’ knees, saying, Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord.
Saying, The Son of man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and the third day rise again.

sing.en: How shall we sing the LORD’s song in a strange land?
In that day sing ye unto her, A vineyard of red wine.

singer.en: The singers: the children of Asaph, an hundred forty and eight.
The singers: the children of Asaph, an hundred twenty and eight.

singing.en: Serve the LORD with gladness: come before his presence with singing.
The whole earth is at rest, and is quiet: they break forth into singing.

single.en: The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.
The light of the body is the eye: therefore when thine eye is single, thy whole body also is full of light; but when thine eye is evil, thy body also is full of darkness.

singleness.en: Servants, obey in all things your masters according to the flesh; not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but in singleness of heart, fearing God:
Servants, be obedient to them that are your masters according to the flesh, with fear and trembling, in singleness of your heart, as unto Christ;

singular.en: Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When a man shall make a singular vow, the persons shall be for the LORD by thy estimation.

sink.en: Let these sayings sink down into your ears: for the Son of man shall be delivered into the hands of men.
I sink in deep mire, where there is no standing: I am come into deep waters, where the floods overflow me.

sinner.en: My son, if sinners entice thee, consent thou not.
We who are Jews by nature, and not sinners of the Gentiles,

sir.en: The nobleman saith unto him, Sir, come down ere my child die.
And brought them out, and said, Sirs, what must I do to be saved?

sister.en: The children of thy elect sister greet thee. Amen.
Now Jesus loved Martha, and her sister, and Lazarus.

sit.en: And they did so, and made them all sit down.
And he commanded the multitude to sit down on the ground.

sith.en: Therefore, as I live, saith the Lord GOD, I will prepare thee unto blood, and blood shall pursue thee: sith thou hast not hated blood, even blood shall pursue thee.

sitting.en: And sitting down they watched him there;
Was returning, and sitting in his chariot read Esaias the prophet.

situate.en: The forefront of the one was situate northward over against Michmash, and the other southward over against Gibeah.
Art thou better than populous No, that was situate among the rivers, that had the waters round about it, whose rampart was the sea, and her wall was from the sea?

situation.en: Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King.
And the men of the city said unto Elisha, Behold, I pray thee, the situation of this city is pleasant, as my lord seeth: but the water is naught, and the ground barren.

sivan.en: Then were the king’s scribes called at that time in the third month, that is, the month Sivan, on the three and twentieth day thereof; and it was written according to all that Mordecai commanded unto the Jews, and to the lieutenants, and the deputies and rulers of the provinces which are from India unto Ethiopia, an hundred twenty and seven provinces, unto every province according to the writing thereof, and unto every people after their language, and to the Jews according to their writing, and according to their language.

six.en: The men of Netophah, fifty and six.
And thirty and six thousand beeves,

sixscore.en: And Hiram sent to the king sixscore talents of gold.
And should not I spare Nineveh, that great city, wherein are more than sixscore thousand persons that cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand; and also much cattle?

sixteen.en: And we were in all in the ship two hundred threescore and sixteen souls.

sixteenth.en: The fifteenth to Bilgah, the sixteenth to Immer,
The sixteenth to Hananiah, he, his sons, and his brethren, were twelve:

sixth.en: Ozem the sixth, David the seventh:
Attai the sixth, Eliel the seventh,

sixty.en: The children of Adonikam, six hundred sixty and six.
And Mahalaleel lived sixty and five years, and begat Jared:

size.en: And the other cherub was ten cubits: both the cherubims were of one measure and one size.
After this manner he made the ten bases: all of them had one casting, one measure, and one size.

skilful.en: And Chenaniah, chief of the Levites, was for song: he instructed about the song, because he was skilful.
And I will pour out mine indignation upon thee, I will blow against thee in the fire of my wrath, and deliver thee into the hand of brutish men, and skilful to destroy.

skill.en: And he informed me, and talked with me, and said, O Daniel, I am now come forth to give thee skill and understanding.
As for these four children, God gave them knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom: and Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams.

skin.en: My skin is black upon me, and my bones are burned with heat.
But if the scall spread much in the skin after his cleansing;

skip.en: He maketh them also to skip like a calf; Lebanon and Sirion like a young unicorn.

skirt.en: A man shall not take his father’s wife, nor discover his father’s skirt.
Thou shalt also take thereof a few in number, and bind them in thy skirts.

skull.en: And when they were come unto a place called Golgotha, that is to say, a place of a skull,
And they bring him unto the place Golgotha, which is, being interpreted, The place of a skull.

sky.en: Hast thou with him spread out the sky, which is strong, and as a molten looking glass?
The clouds poured out water: the skies sent out a sound: thine arrows also went abroad.

slack.en: He becometh poor that dealeth with a slack hand: but the hand of the diligent maketh rich.
In that day it shall be said to Jerusalem, Fear thou not: and to Zion, Let not thine hands be slack.

slackness.en: The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.

slander.en: He that hideth hatred with lying lips, and he that uttereth a slander, is a fool.
Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother’s son.

slanderer.en: Even so must their wives be grave, not slanderers, sober, faithful in all things.

slang.en: And David put his hand in his bag, and took thence a stone, and slang it, and smote the Philistine in his forehead, that the stone sunk into his forehead; and he fell upon his face to the earth.

slaughter.en: Thus saith the LORD my God; Feed the flock of the slaughter;
I will bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams with he goats.

slav.en: And cinnamon, and odours, and ointments, and frankincense, and wine, and oil, and fine flour, and wheat, and beasts, and sheep, and horses, and chariots, and slaves, and souls of men.

slave.en: Is Israel a servant? is he a homeborn slave? why is he spoiled?

slay.en: The wicked watcheth the righteous, and seeketh to slay him.
And I heard a voice saying unto me, Arise, Peter; slay and eat.

slayer.en: But if the slayer shall at any time come without the border of the city of his refuge, whither he was fled;
Then the congregation shall judge between the slayer and the revenger of blood according to these judgments:

sleep.en: Give not sleep to thine eyes, nor slumber to thine eyelids.
And if the man be poor, thou shalt not sleep with his pledge:

sleeper.en: So the shipmaster came to him, and said unto him, What meanest thou, O sleeper? arise, call upon thy God, if so be that God will think upon us, that we perish not.

sleeping.en: Lest coming suddenly he find you sleeping.
And when he rose up from prayer, and was come to his disciples, he found them sleeping for sorrow,

sleight.en: That we henceforth be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the sleight of men, and cunning craftiness, whereby they lie in wait to deceive;

slept.en: While the bridegroom tarried, they all slumbered and slept.
I laid me down and slept; I awaked; for the LORD sustained me.

slew.en: Who smote great nations, and slew mighty kings;
And they slew a bullock, and brought the child to Eli.

slid.en: For Israel slideth back as a backsliding heifer: now the LORD will feed them as a lamb in a large place.

slidden.en: Why then is this people of Jerusalem slidden back by a perpetual backsliding? they hold fast deceit, they refuse to return.

slide.en: The law of his God is in his heart; none of his steps shall slide.
Judge me, O LORD; for I have walked in mine integrity: I have trusted also in the LORD; therefore I shall not slide.

slightly.en: For they have healed the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, Peace, peace; when there is no peace.
They have healed also the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, Peace, peace; when there is no peace.

slime.en: And they said one to another, Go to, let us make brick, and burn them thoroughly. And they had brick for stone, and slime had they for morter.
And when she could not longer hide him, she took for him an ark of bulrushes, and daubed it with slime and with pitch, and put the child therein; and she laid it in the flags by the river’s brink.

sling.en: As he that bindeth a stone in a sling, so is he that giveth honour to a fool.
Among all this people there were seven hundred chosen men lefthanded; every one could sling stones at an hair breadth, and not miss.

slinger.en: And they beat down the cities, and on every good piece of land cast every man his stone, and filled it; and they stopped all the wells of water, and felled all the good trees: only in Kirharaseth left they the stones thereof; howbeit the slingers went about it, and smote it.

slip.en: Hold up my goings in thy paths, that my footsteps slip not.
Thou hast enlarged my steps under me, that my feet did not slip.

slippery.en: Let their way be dark and slippery: and let the angel of the LORD persecute them.
Surely thou didst set them in slippery places: thou castedst them down into destruction.

slothful.en: Not slothful in business; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord;
The desire of the slothful killeth him; for his hands refuse to labour.

slow.en: The LORD is merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and plenteous in mercy.
The LORD is gracious, and full of compassion; slow to anger, and of great mercy.

slowly.en: And when we had sailed slowly many days, and scarce were come over against Cnidus, the wind not suffering us, we sailed under Crete, over against Salmone;

sluggard.en: Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise:
How long wilt thou sleep, O sluggard? when wilt thou arise out of thy sleep?

sluice.en: And they shall be broken in the purposes thereof, all that make sluices and ponds for fish.

slumber.en: While the bridegroom tarried, they all slumbered and slept.
Give not sleep to thine eyes, nor slumber to thine eyelids.

small.en: I am small and despised: yet do not I forget thy precepts.
And the same time there arose no small stir about that way.

smart.en: He that is surety for a stranger shall smart for it: and he that hateth suretiship is sure.

smell.en: They have ears, but they hear not: noses have they, but they smell not:
I hate, I despise your feast days, and I will not smell in your solemn assemblies.

smelling.en: His cheeks are as a bed of spices, as sweet flowers: his lips like lilies, dropping sweet smelling myrrh.
If the whole body were an eye, where were the hearing? If the whole were hearing, where were the smelling?

smit.en: He that smiteth a man, so that he die, shall be surely put to death.
And he that smiteth his father, or his mother, shall be surely put to death.

smite.en: Vex the Midianites, and smite them:
The sun shall not smite thee by day, nor the moon by night.

smiter.en: I gave my back to the smiters, and my cheeks to them that plucked off the hair: I hid not my face from shame and spitting.

smith.en: Now there was no smith found throughout all the land of Israel: for the Philistines said, Lest the Hebrews make them swords or spears:
Behold, I have created the smith that bloweth the coals in the fire, and that bringeth forth an instrument for his work; and I have created the waster to destroy.

smitten.en: But the wheat and the rie were not smitten: for they were not grown up.
And seven days were fulfilled, after that the LORD had smitten the river.

smoke.en: Out of his nostrils goeth smoke, as out of a seething pot or caldron.
And again they said, Alleluia.  And her smoke rose up for ever and ever.

smoking.en: A bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench, till he send forth judgment unto victory.
A bruised reed shall he not break, and the smoking flax shall he not quench: he shall bring forth judgment unto truth.

smooth.en: And she put the skins of the kids of the goats upon his hands, and upon the smooth of his neck:
And Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, Behold, Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man:

smoother.en: For the lips of a strange woman drop as an honeycomb, and her mouth is smoother than oil:
The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart: his words were softer than oil, yet were they drawn swords.

smote.en: Who smote great nations, and slew mighty kings;
And the men that held Jesus mocked him, and smote him.

snail.en: And the ferret, and the chameleon, and the lizard, and the snail, and the mole.
As a snail which melteth, let every one of them pass away: like the untimely birth of a woman, that they may not see the sun.

snar.en: He taketh it with his eyes: his nose pierceth through snares.
Therefore snares are round about thee, and sudden fear troubleth thee;

snare.en: Lest thou learn his ways, and get a snare to thy soul.
And they served their idols: which were a snare unto them.

snatch.en: And he shall snatch on the right hand, and be hungry; and he shall eat on the left hand, and they shall not be satisfied: they shall eat every man the flesh of his own arm:

sneeze.en: Then he returned, and walked in the house to and fro; and went up, and stretched himself upon him: and the child sneezed seven times, and the child opened his eyes.

snort.en: The snorting of his horses was heard from Dan: the whole land trembled at the sound of the neighing of his strong ones; for they are come, and have devoured the land, and all that is in it; the city, and those that dwell therein.

snout.en: As a jewel of gold in a swine’s snout, so is a fair woman which is without discretion.

snow.en: He giveth snow like wool: he scattereth the hoarfrost like ashes.
His countenance was like lightning, and his raiment white as snow:

snowy.en: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the son of a valiant man of Kabzeel, who had done many acts; he slew two lionlike men of Moab: also he went down and slew a lion in a pit in a snowy day.

snuff.en: And the wild asses did stand in the high places, they snuffed up the wind like dragons; their eyes did fail, because there was no grass.

A wild ass used to the wilderness, that snuffeth up the wind at her pleasure; in her occasion who can turn her away? all they that seek her will not weary themselves; in her month they shall find her.

snuffers.en: And he made his seven lamps, and his snuffers, and his snuffdishes, of pure gold.
And the pots, and the shovels, and the snuffers, and the spoons, and all the vessels of brass wherewith they ministered, took they away.

so.en: So Paul departed from among them.
But ye have not so learned Christ;

soak.en: And the unicorns shall come down with them, and the bullocks with the bulls; and their land shall be soaked with blood, and their dust made fat with fatness.

soap.en: For though thou wash thee with nitre, and take thee much soap, yet thine iniquity is marked before me, saith the Lord GOD.
But who may abide the day of his coming? and who shall stand when he appeareth? for he is like a refiner’s fire, and like fullers’ soap:

sober.en: Young men likewise exhort to be sober minded.
Therefore let us not sleep, as do others; but let us watch and be sober.

soberly.en: Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world;

For I say, through the grace given unto me, to every man that is among you, not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly, according as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith.

soberness.en: But he said, I am not mad, most noble Festus; but speak forth the words of truth and soberness.

sobriety.en: Notwithstanding she shall be saved in childbearing, if they continue in faith and charity and holiness with sobriety.
In like manner also, that women adorn themselves in modest apparel, with shamefacedness and sobriety; not with broided hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly array;

socket.en: And the pillars of the court round about, and their sockets, and their pins, and their cords.
And their forty sockets of silver; two sockets under one board, and two sockets under another board.

sod.en: And Jacob sod pottage: and Esau came from the field, and he was faint:
And they roasted the passover with fire according to the ordinance: but the other holy offerings sod they in pots, and in caldrons, and in pans, and divided them speedily among all the people.

sodden.en: Eat not of it raw, nor sodden at all with water, but roast with fire; his head with his legs, and with the purtenance thereof.
The hands of the pitiful women have sodden their own children: they were their meat in the destruction of the daughter of my people.

soder.en: So the carpenter encouraged the goldsmith, and he that smootheth with the hammer him that smote the anvil, saying, It is ready for the sodering: and he fastened it with nails, that it should not be moved.

sodomite.en: There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel, nor a sodomite of the sons of Israel.
And he took away the sodomites out of the land, and removed all the idols that his fathers had made.

soever.en: And what saddle soever he rideth upon that hath the issue shall be unclean.
What thing soever I command you, observe to do it: thou shalt not add thereto, nor diminish from it.

soft.en: For God maketh my heart soft, and the Almighty troubleth me:
A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.

softly.en: Forasmuch as this people refuseth the waters of Shiloah that go softly, and rejoice in Rezin and Remaliah’s son;
And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, loosing thence, they sailed close by Crete.

soil.en: It was planted in a good soil by great waters, that it might bring forth branches, and that it might bear fruit, that it might be a goodly vine.

sojourn.en: And Abraham sojourned in the Philistines’ land many days.
Israel also came into Egypt; and Jacob sojourned in the land of Ham.

sojourner.en: And the Beerothites fled to Gittaim, and were sojourners there until this day.)
The land shall not be sold for ever: for the land is mine; for ye are strangers and sojourners with me.

sojourning.en: Now the sojourning of the children of Israel, who dwelt in Egypt, was four hundred and thirty years.
And if ye call on the Father, who without respect of persons judgeth according to every man’s work, pass the time of your sojourning here in fear:

sol.en: And ye shall tread down the wicked; for they shall be ashes under the soles of your feet in the day that I shall do this, saith the LORD of hosts.
Every place whereon the soles of your feet shall tread shall be yours: from the wilderness and Lebanon, from the river, the river Euphrates, even unto the uttermost sea shall your coast be.

solace.en: Come, let us take our fill of love until the morning: let us solace ourselves with loves.

sold.en: We have drunken our water for money; our wood is sold unto us.
He sent a man before them, even Joseph, who was sold for a servant:

soldier.en: Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ.
Then the soldiers cut off the ropes of the boat, and let her fall off.

sole.en: Every place that the sole of your foot shall tread upon, that have I given unto you, as I said unto Moses.
I have digged, and drunk water; and with the sole of my feet have I dried up all the rivers of the besieged places.

solemn.en: Blow the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly:
And Jehu said, Proclaim a solemn assembly for Baal. And they proclaimed it.

solemnity.en: And Moses commanded them, saying, At the end of every seven years, in the solemnity of the year of release, in the feast of tabernacles,
And in the feasts and in the solemnities the meat offering shall be an ephah to a bullock, and an ephah to a ram, and to the lambs as he is able to give, and an hin of oil to an ephah.

solemnly.en: And Judah spake unto him, saying, The man did solemnly protest unto us, saying, Ye shall not see my face, except your brother be with you.
Now therefore hearken unto their voice: howbeit yet protest solemnly unto them, and shew them the manner of the king that shall reign over them.

solitarily.en: Feed thy people with thy rod, the flock of thine heritage, which dwell solitarily in the wood, in the midst of Carmel: let them feed in Bashan and Gilead, as in the days of old.

solitary.en: Lo, let that night be solitary, let no joyful voice come therein.
They wandered in the wilderness in a solitary way; they found no city to dwell in.

solomon.en: But Solomon built him an house.
And Solomon sent to Hiram, saying,

some.en: For some are already turned aside after Satan.
And of some have compassion, making a difference:

somebody.en: And Jesus said, Somebody hath touched me: for I perceive that virtue is gone out of me.

For before these days rose up Theudas, boasting himself to be somebody; to whom a number of men, about four hundred, joined themselves: who was slain; and all, as many as obeyed him, were scattered, and brought to nought.

something.en: And he gave heed unto them, expecting to receive something of them.
For if a man think himself to be something, when he is nothing, he deceiveth himself.

sometime.en: And you, that were sometime alienated and enemies in your mind by wicked works, yet now hath he reconciled
Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, eight souls were saved by water.

sometimes.en: But now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ.
For ye were sometimes darkness, but now are ye light in the Lord: walk as children of light:

somewhat.en: He said moreover, I have somewhat to say unto thee. And she said, Say on.
Nevertheless I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first love.

son.en: And the sons of Dan; Hushim.
Amon his son, Josiah his son.

song.en: The song of songs, which is Solomon’s.
And now am I their song, yea, I am their byword.

soon.en: They soon forgat his works; they waited not for his counsel:
As soon as she heard that, she arose quickly, and came unto him.

sooner.en: But I beseech you the rather to do this, that I may be restored to you the sooner.

For the sun is no sooner risen with a burning heat, but it withereth the grass, and the flower thereof falleth, and the grace of the fashion of it perisheth: so also shall the rich man fade away in his ways.

soothsayer.en: And I will cut off witchcrafts out of thine hand; and thou shalt have no more soothsayers:
Balaam also the son of Beor, the soothsayer, did the children of Israel slay with the sword among them that were slain by them.

soothsaying.en: And it came to pass, as we went to prayer, a certain damsel possessed with a spirit of divination met us, which brought her masters much gain by soothsaying:

sop.en: He then having received the sop went immediately out: and it was night.
And after the sop Satan entered into him. Then said Jesus unto him, That thou doest, do quickly.

sorcerer.en: For without are dogs, and sorcerers, and whoremongers, and murderers, and idolaters, and whosoever loveth and maketh a lie.
But Elymas the sorcerer (for so is his name by interpretation) withstood them, seeking to turn away the deputy from the faith.

sorceress.en: But draw near hither, ye sons of the sorceress, the seed of the adulterer and the whore.

sorcery.en: And to him they had regard, because that of long time he had bewitched them with sorceries.
Neither repented they of their murders, nor of their sorceries, nor of their fornication, nor of their thefts.

sore.en: And the famine was sore in the land.
The LORD hath been sore displeased with your fathers.

sorely.en: The archers have sorely grieved him, and shot at him, and hated him:
As at the report concerning Egypt, so shall they be sorely pained at the report of Tyre.

sorrow.en: All these are the beginning of sorrows.
Give them sorrow of heart, thy curse unto them.

sorrowed.en: Now I rejoice, not that ye were made sorry, but that ye sorrowed to repentance: for ye were made sorry after a godly manner, that ye might receive damage by us in nothing.

For behold this selfsame thing, that ye sorrowed after a godly sort, what carefulness it wrought in you, yea, what clearing of yourselves, yea, what indignation, yea, what fear, yea, what vehement desire, yea, what zeal, yea, what revenge! In all things ye have approved yourselves to be clear in this matter.

sorrowful.en: The things that my soul refused to touch are as my sorrowful meat.
And when he heard this, he was very sorrowful: for he was very rich.

sorry.en: For I will declare mine iniquity; I will be sorry for my sin.
And they shall kill him, and the third day he shall be raised again. And they were exceeding sorry.

sort.en: He spake, and there came divers sorts of flies, and lice in all their coasts.
Thou shalt not wear a garment of divers sorts, as of woollen and linen together.

sottish.en: For my people is foolish, they have not known me; they are sottish children, and they have none understanding: they are wise to do evil, but to do good they have no knowledge.

sought.en: I am thine, save me; for I have sought thy precepts.
And from that time he sought opportunity to betray him.

soul.en: In your patience possess ye your souls.
Unto thee, O LORD, do I lift up my soul.

sound.en: But speak thou the things which become sound doctrine:
A sound of battle is in the land, and of great destruction.

sounding.en: Praise him upon the loud cymbals: praise him upon the high sounding cymbals.
Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal.

soundness.en: For my loins are filled with a loathsome disease: and there is no soundness in my flesh.
There is no soundness in my flesh because of thine anger; neither is there any rest in my bones because of my sin.

sour.en: Their drink is sour: they have committed whoredom continually: her rulers with shame do love, Give ye.
But every one shall die for his own iniquity: every man that eateth the sour grape, his teeth shall be set on edge.

south.en: And Abram journeyed, going on still toward the south.
Turn again our captivity, O LORD, as the streams in the south.

southward.en: To Obededom southward; and to his sons the house of Asuppim.
And he made boards for the tabernacle; twenty boards for the south side southward:

sow.en: They that sow in tears shall reap in joy.

sower.en: Hear ye therefore the parable of the sower.

sown.en: And these are they which are sown among thorns; such as hear the word,
Light is sown for the righteous, and gladness for the upright in heart.

space.en: And I gave her space to repent of her fornication; and she repented not.
And it was about the space of three hours after, when his wife, not knowing what was done, came in.

span.en: Foursquare it shall be being doubled; a span shall be the length thereof, and a span shall be the breadth thereof.
And there went out a champion out of the camp of the Philistines, named Goliath, of Gath, whose height was six cubits and a span.

spar.en: He coveteth greedily all the day long: but the righteous giveth and spareth not.
For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee.

spare.en: They abhor me, they flee far from me, and spare not to spit in my face.
He shall spare the poor and needy, and shall save the souls of the needy.

sparing.en: For I know this, that after my departing shall grievous wolves enter in among you, not sparing the flock.

spark.en: Yet man is born unto trouble, as the sparks fly upward.
Out of his mouth go burning lamps, and sparks of fire leap out.

sparkle.en: And their feet were straight feet; and the sole of their feet was like the sole of a calf’s foot: and they sparkled like the colour of burnished brass.

sparrow.en: I watch, and am as a sparrow alone upon the house top.
Fear ye not therefore, ye are of more value than many sparrows.

spat.en: When he had thus spoken, he spat on the ground, and made clay of the spittle, and he anointed the eyes of the blind man with the clay,

speak.en: I speak as to wise men; judge ye what I say.
That I may make it manifest, as I ought to speak.

speaker.en: And they called Barnabas, Jupiter; and Paul, Mercurius, because he was the chief speaker.
Let not an evil speaker be established in the earth: evil shall hunt the violent man to overthrow him.

speaking.en: Keep thy tongue from evil, and thy lips from speaking guile.
And Moses made an end of speaking all these words to all Israel:

spear.en: Darts are counted as stubble: he laugheth at the shaking of a spear.
The quiver rattleth against him, the glittering spear and the shield.

special.en: And God wrought special miracles by the hands of Paul:
For thou art an holy people unto the LORD thy God: the LORD thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.

specially.en: For there are many unruly and vain talkers and deceivers, specially they of the circumcision:
But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.

speckled.en: And the flocks conceived before the rods, and brought forth cattle ringstraked, speckled, and spotted.
Mine heritage is unto me as a speckled bird, the birds round about are against her; come ye, assemble all the beasts of the field, come to devour.

spectacle.en: For I think that God hath set forth us the apostles last, as it were appointed to death: for we are made a spectacle unto the world, and to angels, and to men.

sped.en: Have they not sped? have they not divided the prey; to every man a damsel or two; to Sisera a prey of divers colours, a prey of divers colours of needlework, of divers colours of needlework on both sides, meet for the necks of them that take the spoil?

speech.en: And the whole earth was of one language, and of one speech.
Give ye ear, and hear my voice; hearken, and hear my speech.

speechless.en: And the men which journeyed with him stood speechless, hearing a voice, but seeing no man.
And he saith unto him, Friend, how camest thou in hither not having a wedding garment? And he was speechless.

speed.en: For he that biddeth him God speed is partaker of his evil deeds.
If there come any unto you, and bring not this doctrine, receive him not into your house, neither bid him God speed:

speedily.en: And hide not thy face from thy servant; for I am in trouble: hear me speedily.
Then they speedily took down every man his sack to the ground, and opened every man his sack.

speedy.en: Neither their silver nor their gold shall be able to deliver them in the day of the LORD’s wrath; but the whole land shall be devoured by the fire of his jealousy: for he shall make even a speedy riddance of all them that dwell in the land.

spend.en: I will heap mischiefs upon them; I will spend mine arrows upon them.
They spend their days in wealth, and in a moment go down to the grave.

spent.en: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, and are spent without hope.
And the water was spent in the bottle, and she cast the child under one of the shrubs.

spew.en: Thou art filled with shame for glory: drink thou also, and let thy foreskin be uncovered: the cup of the LORD’s right hand shall be turned unto thee, and shameful spewing shall be on thy glory.

spice.en: Oil for the light, spices for anointing oil, and for sweet incense,
And some of the sons of the priests made the ointment of the spices.

spicery.en: And they sat down to eat bread: and they lifted up their eyes and looked, and, behold, a company of Ishmeelites came from Gilead with their camels bearing spicery and balm and myrrh, going to carry it down to Egypt.

spider.en: The spider taketh hold with her hands, and is in kings’ palaces.
Whose hope shall be cut off, and whose trust shall be a spider’s web.

spied.en: But Joshua had said unto the two men that had spied out the country, Go into the harlot’s house, and bring out thence the woman, and all that she hath, as ye sware unto her.
And it came to pass in those days, when Moses was grown, that he went out unto his brethren, and looked on their burdens: and he spied an Egyptian smiting an Hebrew, one of his brethren.

spikenard.en: While the king sitteth at his table, my spikenard sendeth forth the smell thereof.
Thy plants are an orchard of pomegranates, with pleasant fruits; camphire, with spikenard,

spill.en: And no man putteth new wine into old bottles; else the new wine will burst the bottles, and be spilled, and the bottles shall perish.
And no man putteth new wine into old bottles: else the new wine doth burst the bottles, and the wine is spilled, and the bottles will be marred: but new wine must be put into new bottles.

spilt.en: For we must needs die, and are as water spilt on the ground, which cannot be gathered up again; neither doth God respect any person: yet doth he devise means, that his banished be not expelled from him.

spin.en: And why take ye thought for raiment? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin:
Consider the lilies how they grow: they toil not, they spin not; and yet I say unto you, that Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.

spindle.en: She layeth her hands to the spindle, and her hands hold the distaff.

spirit.en: And be renewed in the spirit of your mind;

spiritual.en: And did all eat the same spiritual meat;
For we know that the law is spiritual: but I am carnal, sold under sin.

spiritually.en: For to be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace.
And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.

spit.en: And they spit upon him, and took the reed, and smote him on the head.
They abhor me, they flee far from me, and spare not to spit in my face.

spite.en: Thou hast seen it; for thou beholdest mischief and spite, to requite it with thy hand: the poor committeth himself unto thee; thou art the helper of the fatherless.

spitted.en: For he shall be delivered unto the Gentiles, and shall be mocked, and spitefully entreated, and spitted on:

spittle.en: How long wilt thou not depart from me, nor let me alone till I swallow down my spittle?
When he had thus spoken, he spat on the ground, and made clay of the spittle, and he anointed the eyes of the blind man with the clay,

spoil.en: I rejoice at thy word, as one that findeth great spoil.
They rewarded me evil for good to the spoiling of my soul.

spoiler.en: Then the heaven and the earth, and all that is therein, shall sing for Babylon: for the spoilers shall come unto her from the north, saith the LORD.
And the LORD rejected all the seed of Israel, and afflicted them, and delivered them into the hand of spoilers, until he had cast them out of his sight.

spoke.en: And the work of the wheels was like the work of a chariot wheel: their axletrees, and their naves, and their felloes, and their spokes, were all molten.

spoken.en: Let not then your good be evil spoken of:
For the LORD had spoken unto Moses, saying,

spokesman.en: And he shall be thy spokesman unto the people: and he shall be, even he shall be to thee instead of a mouth, and thou shalt be to him instead of God.

spoon.en: One golden spoon of ten shekels, full of incense:
One golden spoon of ten shekels, full of incense:

sport.en: So is the man that deceiveth his neighbour, and saith, Am not I in sport?
It is as sport to a fool to do mischief: but a man of understanding hath wisdom.

sporting.en: And it came to pass, when he had been there a long time, that Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out at a window, and saw, and, behold, Isaac was sporting with Rebekah his wife.

And shall receive the reward of unrighteousness, as they that count it pleasure to riot in the day time. Spots they are and blemishes, sporting themselves with their own deceivings while they feast with you;

spot.en: Thou art all fair, my love; there is no spot in thee.
And for a rising, and for a scab, and for a bright spot:

spotted.en: And the flocks conceived before the rods, and brought forth cattle ringstraked, speckled, and spotted.
And others save with fear, pulling them out of the fire; hating even the garment spotted by the flesh.

spouse.en: A garden inclosed is my sister, my spouse; a spring shut up, a fountain sealed.
Thou hast ravished my heart, my sister, my spouse; thou hast ravished my heart with one of thine eyes, with one chain of thy neck.

sprang.en: And some fell among thorns; and the thorns sprang up with it, and choked it.
Then he called for a light, and sprang in, and came trembling, and fell down before Paul and Silas,

spread.en: And as he went, they spread their clothes in the way.
Surely in vain the net is spread in the sight of any bird.

sprig.en: For afore the harvest, when the bud is perfect, and the sour grape is ripening in the flower, he shall both cut off the sprigs with pruning hooks, and take away and cut down the branches.

And it grew, and became a spreading vine of low stature, whose branches turned toward him, and the roots thereof were under him: so it became a vine, and brought forth branches, and shot forth sprigs.

spring.en: Then Israel sang this song, Spring up, O well; sing ye unto it:
He sendeth the springs into the valleys, which run among the hills.

springing.en: And Isaac’s servants digged in the valley, and found there a well of springing water.
Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled;

sprinkle.en: And he killed it; and Moses sprinkled the blood upon the altar round about.
Moreover he sprinkled with blood both the tabernacle, and all the vessels of the ministry.

sprinkling.en: Through faith he kept the passover, and the sprinkling of blood, lest he that destroyed the firstborn should touch them.
And to Jesus the mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling, that speaketh better things than that of Abel.

sprout.en: For there is hope of a tree, if it be cut down, that it will sprout again, and that the tender branch thereof will not cease.

sprung.en: And some fell among thorns; and the thorns sprung up, and choked them:
And, behold, seven thin ears and blasted with the east wind sprung up after them.

spue.en: So then because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spue thee out of my mouth.
That the land spue not you out also, when ye defile it, as it spued out the nations that were before you.

spun.en: And all the women whose heart stirred them up in wisdom spun goats’ hair.
And all the women that were wise hearted did spin with their hands, and brought that which they had spun, both of blue, and of purple, and of scarlet, and of fine linen.

spunge.en: And straightway one of them ran, and took a spunge, and filled it with vinegar, and put it on a reed, and gave him to drink.
Now there was set a vessel full of vinegar: and they filled a spunge with vinegar, and put it upon hyssop, and put it to his mouth.

spy.en: And we said unto him, We are true men; we are no spies:
We are all one man’s sons; we are true men, thy servants are no spies.

square.en: And the altar shall be twelve cubits long, twelve broad, square in the four squares thereof.
And all the doors and posts were square, with the windows: and light was against light in three ranks.

stability.en: And wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times, and strength of salvation: the fear of the LORD is his treasure.

stable.en: Fear before him, all the earth: the world also shall be stable, that it be not moved.
And I will make Rabbah a stable for camels, and the Ammonites a couching place for flocks: and ye shall know that I am the LORD.

stablish.en: Stablish thy word unto thy servant, who is devoted to thy fear.
Comfort your hearts, and stablish you in every good word and work.

stack.en: If fire break out, and catch in thorns, so that the stacks of corn, or the standing corn, or the field, be consumed therewith; he that kindled the fire shall surely make restitution.

stacte.en: And the LORD said unto Moses, Take unto thee sweet spices, stacte, and onycha, and galbanum; these sweet spices with pure frankincense: of each shall there be a like weight:

staff.en: The LORD hath broken the staff of the wicked, and the sceptre of the rulers.
Moreover he called for a famine upon the land: he brake the whole staff of bread.

stagger.en: They reel to and fro, and stagger like a drunken man, and are at their wit’s end.
They grope in the dark without light, and he maketh them to stagger like a drunken man.

stain.en: Let darkness and the shadow of death stain it; let a cloud dwell upon it; let the blackness of the day terrify it.
The LORD of hosts hath purposed it, to stain the pride of all glory, and to bring into contempt all the honourable of the earth.

stair.en: And when he came upon the stairs, so it was, that he was borne of the soldiers for the violence of the people.
Then they hasted, and took every man his garment, and put it under him on the top of the stairs, and blew with trumpets, saying, Jehu is king.

stake.en: Enlarge the place of thy tent, and let them stretch forth the curtains of thine habitations: spare not, lengthen thy cords, and strengthen thy stakes;

Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities: thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down; not one of the stakes thereof shall ever be removed, neither shall any of the cords thereof be broken.

stalk.en: And I saw in my dream, and, behold, seven ears came up in one stalk, full and good:
And he slept and dreamed the second time: and, behold, seven ears of corn came up upon one stalk, rank and good.

stall.en: And Solomon had forty thousand stalls of horses for his chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen.
Storehouses also for the increase of corn, and wine, and oil; and stalls for all manner of beasts, and cotes for flocks.

stalled.en: Better is a dinner of herbs where love is, than a stalled ox and hatred therewith.

stammerer.en: The heart also of the rash shall understand knowledge, and the tongue of the stammerers shall be ready to speak plainly.

stammering.en: For with stammering lips and another tongue will he speak to this people.
Thou shalt not see a fierce people, a people of a deeper speech than thou canst perceive; of a stammering tongue, that thou canst not understand.

stamp.en: Then did I beat them as small as the dust of the earth, I did stamp them as the mire of the street, and did spread them abroad.
And it waxed great, even to the host of heaven; and it cast down some of the host and of the stars to the ground, and stamped upon them.

stamping.en: At the noise of the stamping of the hoofs of his strong horses, at the rushing of his chariots, and at the rumbling of his wheels, the fathers shall not look back to their children for feebleness of hands;

stanch.en: Came behind him, and touched the border of his garment: and immediately her issue of blood stanched.

stand.en: And why stand we in jeopardy every hour?
For now we live, if ye stand fast in the Lord.

standard.en: How long shall I see the standard, and hear the sound of the trumpet?
Set up the standard toward Zion: retire, stay not: for I will bring evil from the north, and a great destruction.

standing.en: And he made boards for the tabernacle of shittim wood, standing up.
And thou shalt make boards for the tabernacle of shittim wood standing up.

stank.en: And they gathered them together upon heaps: and the land stank.
Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto Moses; but some of them left of it until the morning, and it bred worms, and stank: and Moses was wroth with them.

star.en: And I will give him the morning star.
When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceeding great joy.

stare.en: I may tell all my bones: they look and stare upon me.

state.en: For I have no man likeminded, who will naturally care for your state.
Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, and look well to thy herds.

stately.en: And satest upon a stately bed, and a table prepared before it, whereupon thou hast set mine incense and mine oil.

station.en: And I will drive thee from thy station, and from thy state shall he pull thee down.

stature.en: Which of you by taking thought can add one cubit unto his stature?
And which of you with taking thought can add to his stature one cubit?

statute.en: Blessed art thou, O LORD: teach me thy statutes.
O that my ways were directed to keep thy statutes!

staves.en: And he made staves of shittim wood, and overlaid them with gold.
The table, and his staves, and all his vessels, and the shewbread,

stay.en: Stay me with flagons, comfort me with apples: for I am sick of love.
They prevented me in the day of my calamity: but the LORD was my stay.

stayed.en: And he stood between the dead and the living; and the plague was stayed.
Then stood up Phinehas, and executed judgment: and so the plague was stayed.

stead.en: And Hadad died, and Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his stead.
And when Hadad was dead, Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his stead.

steady.en: But Moses’ hands were heavy; and they took a stone, and put it under him, and he sat thereon; and Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side; and his hands were steady until the going down of the sun.

stealing.en: By swearing, and lying, and killing, and stealing, and committing adultery, they break out, and blood toucheth blood.
If a man be found stealing any of his brethren of the children of Israel, and maketh merchandise of him, or selleth him; then that thief shall die; and thou shalt put evil away from among you.

stealth.en: And the people gat them by stealth that day into the city, as people being ashamed steal away when they flee in battle.

stedfast.en: For their heart was not right with him, neither were they stedfast in his covenant.
For then shalt thou lift up thy face without spot; yea, thou shalt be stedfast, and shalt not fear:

stedfastly.en: And he settled his countenance stedfastly, until he was ashamed: and the man of God wept.
When she saw that she was stedfastly minded to go with her, then she left speaking unto her.

steel.en: Shall iron break the northern iron and the steel?
He teacheth my hands to war; so that a bow of steel is broken by mine arms.

steep.en: Then went the devils out of the man, and entered into the swine: and the herd ran violently down a steep place into the lake, and were choked.
And the mountains shall be molten under him, and the valleys shall be cleft, as wax before the fire, and as the waters that are poured down a steep place.

stem.en: And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots:

step.en: Doth not he see my ways, and count all my steps?
Her feet go down to death; her steps take hold on hell.

steppe.en: The impotent man answered him, Sir, I have no man, when the water is troubled, to put me into the pool: but while I am coming, another steppeth down before me.

stepped.en: For an angel went down at a certain season into the pool, and troubled the water: whosoever then first after the troubling of the water stepped in was made whole of whatsoever disease he had.

stern.en: Then fearing lest we should have fallen upon rocks, they cast four anchors out of the stern, and wished for the day.

steward.en: Moreover it is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful.
Let a man so account of us, as of the ministers of Christ, and stewards of the mysteries of God.

stewardship.en: I am resolved what to do, that, when I am put out of the stewardship, they may receive me into their houses.
Then the steward said within himself, What shall I do? for my lord taketh away from me the stewardship: I cannot dig; to beg I am ashamed.

stick.en: For thine arrows stick fast in me, and thy hand presseth me sore.
And the sticks whereon thou writest shall be in thine hand before their eyes.

stiff.en: Lift not up your horn on high: speak not with a stiff neck.
But they obeyed not, neither inclined their ear, but made their neck stiff, that they might not hear, nor receive instruction.

stiffen.en: And he also rebelled against king Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear by God: but he stiffened his neck, and hardened his heart from turning unto the LORD God of Israel.

still.en: And Abram journeyed, going on still toward the south.
Notwithstanding it pleased Silas to abide there still.

sting.en: O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory?
The sting of death is sin; and the strength of sin is the law.

stink.en: My wounds stink and are corrupt because of my foolishness.
And they laid it up till the morning, as Moses bade: and it did not stink, neither was there any worm therein.

stinking.en: Dead flies cause the ointment of the apothecary to send forth a stinking savour: so doth a little folly him that is in reputation for wisdom and honour.

stir.en: And the same time there arose no small stir about that way.
A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.

stock.en: He putteth my feet in the stocks, he marketh all my paths.
But they are altogether brutish and foolish: the stock is a doctrine of vanities.

stole.en: Saying, Say ye, His disciples came by night, and stole him away while we slept.
And Jacob stole away unawares to Laban the Syrian, in that he told him not that he fled.

stolen.en: Stolen waters are sweet, and bread eaten in secret is pleasant.
And if it be stolen from him, he shall make restitution unto the owner thereof.

stomach.en: Drink no longer water, but use a little wine for thy stomach’s sake and thine often infirmities.

stomacher.en: And it shall come to pass, that instead of sweet smell there shall be stink; and instead of a girdle a rent; and instead of well set hair baldness; and instead of a stomacher a girding of sackcloth; and burning instead of beauty.

stone.en: Then the Jews took up stones again to stone him.
And Jacob took a stone, and set it up for a pillar.

stony.en: When their judges are overthrown in stony places, they shall hear my words; for they are sweet.
But he that received the seed into stony places, the same is he that heareth the word, and anon with joy receiveth it;

stood.en: And they that stood by said, Revilest thou God’s high priest?
Again the next day after John stood, and two of his disciples;

stool.en: And he said, When ye do the office of a midwife to the Hebrew women, and see them upon the stools; if it be a son, then ye shall kill him: but if it be a daughter, then she shall live.

Let us make a little chamber, I pray thee, on the wall; and let us set for him there a bed, and a table, and a stool, and a candlestick: and it shall be, when he cometh to us, that he shall turn in thither.

stoop.en: And again he stooped down, and wrote on the ground.
If God will not withdraw his anger, the proud helpers do stoop under him.

stooping.en: And he stooping down, and looking in, saw the linen clothes lying; yet went he not in.
Then arose Peter, and ran unto the sepulchre; and stooping down, he beheld the linen clothes laid by themselves, and departed, wondering in himself at that which was come to pass.

stop.en: The righteous shall see it, and rejoice: and all iniquity shall stop her mouth.
As the truth of Christ is in me, no man shall stop me of this boasting in the regions of Achaia.

stopped.en: Then they cried out with a loud voice, and stopped their ears, and ran upon him with one accord,
Who through faith subdued kingdoms, wrought righteousness, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions,

store.en: Cursed shall be thy basket and thy store.
Blessed shall be thy basket and thy store.

storehouse.en: He gathereth the waters of the sea together as an heap: he layeth up the depth in storehouses.
Storehouses also for the increase of corn, and wine, and oil; and stalls for all manner of beasts, and cotes for flocks.

stork.en: And the stork, the heron after her kind, and the lapwing, and the bat.
And the stork, and the heron after her kind, and the lapwing, and the bat.

storm.en: I would hasten my escape from the windy storm and tempest.
He maketh the storm a calm, so that the waves thereof are still.

stormy.en: Fire, and hail; snow, and vapours; stormy wind fulfilling his word:
For he commandeth, and raiseth the stormy wind, which lifteth up the waves thereof.

story.en: And the rest of the acts of Abijah, and his ways, and his sayings, are written in the story of the prophet Iddo.
Over against the twenty cubits which were for the inner court, and over against the pavement which was for the utter court, was gallery against gallery in three stories.

stout.en: The old lion perisheth for lack of prey, and the stout lion’s whelps are scattered abroad.
Your words have been stout against me, saith the LORD. Yet ye say, What have we spoken so much against thee?

stoutness.en: And all the people shall know, even Ephraim and the inhabitant of Samaria, that say in the pride and stoutness of heart,

straight.en: Let thine eyes look right on, and let thine eyelids look straight before thee.
Consider the work of God: for who can make that straight, which he hath made crooked?

straightway.en: And they straightway left their nets, and followed him.
And straightway they forsook their nets, and followed him.

strain.en: Ye blind guides, which strain at a gnat, and swallow a camel.

strait.en: In the fulness of his sufficiency he shall be in straits: every hand of the wicked shall come upon him.
For I am in a strait betwixt two, having a desire to depart, and to be with Christ; which is far better:

straiten.en: Ye are not straitened in us, but ye are straitened in your own bowels.
By the breath of God frost is given: and the breadth of the waters is straitened.

straitly.en: And he straitly charged him, and forthwith sent him away;
And he straitly charged them that they should not make him known.

straitness.en: Even so would he have removed thee out of the strait into a broad place, where there is no straitness; and that which should be set on thy table should be full of fatness.

And thou shalt eat the fruit of thine own body, the flesh of thy sons and of thy daughters, which the LORD thy God hath given thee, in the siege, and in the straitness, wherewith thine enemies shall distress thee:

strake.en: Which when they had taken up, they used helps, undergirding the ship; and, fearing lest they should fall into the quicksands, strake sail, and so were driven.
And Jacob took him rods of green poplar, and of the hazel and chestnut tree; and pilled white strakes in them, and made the white appear which was in the rods.

strange.en: How shall we sing the LORD’s song in a strange land?
For a whore is a deep ditch; and a strange woman is a narrow pit.

strangely.en: Were it not that I feared the wrath of the enemy, lest their adversaries should behave themselves strangely, and lest they should say, Our hand is high, and the LORD hath not done all this.

stranger.en: When ye were but few, even a few, and strangers in it.
Let them be only thine own, and not strangers’ with thee.

strangle.en: So that my soul chooseth strangling, and death rather than my life.
But that we write unto them, that they abstain from pollutions of idols, and from fornication, and from things strangled, and from blood.

straw.en: He esteemeth iron as straw, and brass as rotten wood.
Go ye, get you straw where ye can find it: yet not ought of your work shall be diminished.

strawed.en: And many spread their garments in the way: and others cut down branches off the trees, and strawed them in the way.
And a very great multitude spread their garments in the way; others cut down branches from the trees, and strawed them in the way.

stream.en: Turn again our captivity, O LORD, as the streams in the south.
Then the waters had overwhelmed us, the stream had gone over our soul:

street.en: Wisdom crieth without; she uttereth her voice in the streets:
Let thy fountains be dispersed abroad, and rivers of waters in the streets.

strength.en: I will love thee, O LORD, my strength.
Seek the LORD, and his strength: seek his face evermore.

strengthen.en: I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
Strengthen ye the weak hands, and confirm the feeble knees.

strengthening.en: And there appeared an angel unto him from heaven, strengthening him.
And after he had spent some time there, he departed, and went over all the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples.

stretch.en: Thou stretchedst out thy right hand, the earth swallowed them.
If thou prepare thine heart, and stretch out thine hands toward him;

stretching.en: By stretching forth thine hand to heal; and that signs and wonders may be done by the name of thy holy child Jesus.
And he shall pass through Judah; he shall overflow and go over, he shall reach even to the neck; and the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of thy land, O Immanuel.

stricken.en: My son, if thou be surety for thy friend, if thou hast stricken thy hand with a stranger,
And Abraham was old, and well stricken in age: and the LORD had blessed Abraham in all things.

strife.en: Hatred stirreth up strifes: but love covereth all sins.
A froward man soweth strife: and a whisperer separateth chief friends.

strike.en: He striketh them as wicked men in the open sight of others;
Also to punish the just is not good, nor to strike princes for equity.

striker.en: Not given to wine, no striker, not greedy of filthy lucre; but patient, not a brawler, not covetous;
For a bishop must be blameless, as the steward of God; not selfwilled, not soon angry, not given to wine, no striker, not given to filthy lucre;

string.en: Praise the LORD with harp: sing unto him with the psaltery and an instrument of ten strings.
Upon an instrument of ten strings, and upon the psaltery; upon the harp with a solemn sound.

stringed.en: Praise him with the timbrel and dance: praise him with stringed instruments and organs.
The LORD was ready to save me: therefore we will sing my songs to the stringed instruments all the days of our life in the house of the LORD.

strip.en: Of the Jews five times received I forty stripes save one.
Judgments are prepared for scorners, and stripes for the back of fools.

stripe.en: Burning for burning, wound for wound, stripe for stripe.

stripling.en: And the king said, Enquire thou whose son the stripling is.

strive.en: Strive not with a man without cause, if he have done thee no harm.
Why dost thou strive against him? for he giveth not account of any of his matters.

strived.en: Yea, so have I strived to preach the gospel, not where Christ was named, lest I should build upon another man’s foundation:

striven.en: I have laid a snare for thee, and thou art also taken, O Babylon, and thou wast not aware: thou art found, and also caught, because thou hast striven against the LORD.

striving.en: Ye have not yet resisted unto blood, striving against sin.
Whereunto I also labour, striving according to his working, which worketh in me mightily.

stroke.en: A fool’s lips enter into contention, and his mouth calleth for strokes.
Remove thy stroke away from me: I am consumed by the blow of thine hand.

strong.en: How say ye, We are mighty and strong men for the war?
I am as a wonder unto many; but thou art my strong refuge.

strongly.en: In the first year of Cyrus the king the same Cyrus the king made a decree concerning the house of God at Jerusalem, Let the house be builded, the place where they offered sacrifices, and let the foundations thereof be strongly laid; the height thereof threescore cubits, and the breadth thereof threescore cubits;

strove.en: And they digged another well, and strove for that also: and he called the name of it Sitnah.
The Jews therefore strove among themselves, saying, How can this man give us his flesh to eat?

strow.en: And they brake down the altars of Baalim in his presence; and the images, that were on high above them, he cut down; and the groves, and the carved images, and the molten images, he brake in pieces, and made dust of them, and strowed it upon the graves of them that had sacrificed unto them.

struck.en: Neither did Jeroboam recover strength again in the days of Abijah: and the LORD struck him, and he died.
And Nathan departed unto his house. And the LORD struck the child that Uriah’s wife bare unto David, and it was very sick.

struggle.en: And the children struggled together within her; and she said, If it be so, why am I thus? And she went to enquire of the LORD.

stubble.en: O my God, make them like a wheel; as the stubble before the wind.
Darts are counted as stubble: he laugheth at the shaking of a spear.

stubborn.en: (She is loud and stubborn; her feet abide not in her house:
And they shall say unto the elders of his city, This our son is stubborn and rebellious, he will not obey our voice; he is a glutton, and a drunkard.

stuck.en: I have stuck unto thy testimonies: O LORD, put me not to shame.
And falling into a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; and the forepart stuck fast, and remained unmoveable, but the hinder part was broken with the violence of the waves.

stud.en: We will make thee borders of gold with studs of silver.

study.en: And that ye study to be quiet, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands, as we commanded you;
Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.

stuff.en: Also regard not your stuff; for the good of all the land of Egypt is yours.
For the stuff they had was sufficient for all the work to make it, and too much.

stumble.en: Then shalt thou walk in thy way safely, and thy foot shall not stumble.
The way of the wicked is as darkness: they know not at what they stumble.

stump.en: And whereas they commanded to leave the stump of the tree roots; thy kingdom shall be sure unto thee, after that thou shalt have known that the heavens do rule.

Nevertheless leave the stump of his roots in the earth, even with a band of iron and brass, in the tender grass of the field; and let it be wet with the dew of heaven, and let his portion be with the beasts in the grass of the earth:

subdue.en: It is God that avengeth me, and subdueth the people under me.
He shall subdue the people under us, and the nations under our feet.

subdued.en: So God subdued on that day Jabin the king of Canaan before the children of Israel.
I should soon have subdued their enemies, and turned my hand against their adversaries.

subject.en: And the spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets.
Wherefore ye must needs be subject, not only for wrath, but also for conscience sake.

subjected.en: For the creature was made subject to vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him who hath subjected the same in hope,

subjection.en: Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection.
For unto the angels hath he not put in subjection the world to come, whereof we speak.

submit.en: Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord.
Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as it is fit in the Lord.

suborn.en: Then they suborned men, which said, We have heard him speak blasphemous words against Moses, and against God.

subscribe.en: And I subscribed the evidence, and sealed it, and took witnesses, and weighed him the money in the balances.
One shall say, I am the LORD’s; and another shall call himself by the name of Jacob; and another shall subscribe with his hand unto the LORD, and surname himself by the name of Israel.

substance.en: He made him lord of his house, and ruler of all his substance:
Did I say, Bring unto me? or, Give a reward for me of your substance?

subtilty.en: And consulted that they might take Jesus by subtilty, and kill him.
To give subtilty to the simple, to the young man knowledge and discretion.

suburb.en: And Hilen with her suburbs, Debir with her suburbs,
And Ramoth with her suburbs, and Anem with her suburbs:

subvert.en: To subvert a man in his cause, the LORD approveth not.
Knowing that he that is such is subverted, and sinneth, being condemned of himself.

succeed.en: A people great, and many, and tall, as the Anakims; but the LORD destroyed them before them; and they succeeded them, and dwelt in their stead:
And it shall be, that the firstborn which she beareth shall succeed in the name of his brother which is dead, that his name be not put out of Israel.

success.en: This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.

succour.en: For in that he himself hath suffered being tempted, he is able to succour them that are tempted.
And when the Syrians of Damascus came to succour Hadadezer king of Zobah, David slew of the Syrians two and twenty thousand men.

succoured.en: (For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.)

But Abishai the son of Zeruiah succoured him, and smote the Philistine, and killed him. Then the men of David sware unto him, saying, Thou shalt go no more out with us to battle, that thou quench not the light of Israel.

succourer.en: That ye receive her in the Lord, as becometh saints, and that ye assist her in whatsoever business she hath need of you: for she hath been a succourer of many, and of myself also.

such.en: And such trust have we through Christ to God-ward:
Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.

suck.en: Why did the knees prevent me? or why the breasts that I should suck?
He shall suck the poison of asps: the viper’s tongue shall slay him.

sucking.en: And the sucking child shall play on the hole of the asp, and the weaned child shall put his hand on the cockatrice’ den.
The tongue of the sucking child cleaveth to the roof of his mouth for thirst: the young children ask bread, and no man breaketh it unto them.

suckling.en: The sword without, and terror within, shall destroy both the young man and the virgin, the suckling also with the man of gray hairs.
Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings hast thou ordained strength because of thine enemies, that thou mightest still the enemy and the avenger.

sudden.en: Therefore snares are round about thee, and sudden fear troubleth thee;
Be not afraid of sudden fear, neither of the desolation of the wicked, when it cometh.

sue.en: And if any man will sue thee at the law, and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloak also.

suffer.en: Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live.
For ye suffer fools gladly, seeing ye yourselves are wise.

suffering.en: For as the sufferings of Christ abound in us, so our consolation also aboundeth by Christ.
For this is thankworthy, if a man for conscience toward God endure grief, suffering wrongfully.

suffice.en: Philip saith unto him, Lord, shew us the Father, and it sufficeth us.
Shall the flocks and the herds be slain for them, to suffice them? or shall all the fish of the sea be gathered together for them, to suffice them?

sufficiency.en: In the fulness of his sufficiency he shall be in straits: every hand of the wicked shall come upon him.
Not that we are sufficient of ourselves to think any thing as of ourselves; but our sufficiency is of God;

sufficient.en: Sufficient to such a man is this punishment, which was inflicted of many.
For the stuff they had was sufficient for all the work to make it, and too much.

sufficiently.en: For they could not keep it at that time, because the priests had not sanctified themselves sufficiently, neither had the people gathered themselves together to Jerusalem.
